metadata.title: Translation invariant pure state on $\otimes_{\IZ}\!M_d(\IC)$ and Haag duality

extraction_notes.note: The paper has no \label/\ref; every cross-reference is in words, and numbering is inconsistent ("Theorem 2.4/3.4/3.5" mean Propositions 2.4/3.4/3.5; "Theorem 2.6 (a)" in the proof of Theorem 1.1 must mean Theorem 3.6(a)). All uses edges were added by hand to the intended nodes.
Marked origin external because the paper attributes them to Popescu/BJKW ("we recall", "easy adaptations of results proved in [BJKW]") although it gives its own proofs; the proofs are origin paper.
open_problem rather than problem: questions the paper raises in prose and then answers (fully or for pure states) with Theorem 1.1/3.6, recorded by resolves edges.

Repeated statements kept once: BJKW Lemma 7.4 (intro copy dropped for Proposition 2.6), the Section 3 repeat of the dual Popescu elements and KMS relations (equation (29) kept as an equation node), the intro sketch of Popescu dilation (Theorem 2.1 kept), and the three mentions of the type-I/III dichotomy. Weak isomorphism and other historical discussion not used later were not extracted.

The key arguments are page-long transfinite constructions (strict partial orders on quasi-equivalent representations plus Hausdorff maximality); the run-in conditions (C1)-(C3), (C3'), (C3'') became labelled child steps inside the case or claim steps that introduce them.
These prose nodes end at \end{equation} because the author never punctuates after displays; the finishing step's ends-mid-sentence warning is a false alarm.

Every paragraph starts with \vskip 1em, so the sentence-start check flags nearly all steps and prose nodes (warnings left); two steps starting with '(c)' or '$\omega$' were flagged as errors, so their statements keep the leading \vskip 1em.
The type-I Haag-duality claim includes the following 'In fact ...' sentence (the tensor splitting it asserts); the proof starts at 'A simple proof goes as follows:'.

metadata.extraction_comment: Remaining 'factor' defined-term warnings for DP1 are uses of 'factor' in the von Neumann algebra sense (M is a factor), not factor states, and were left without edges.

nodes.name: Factor state
nodes.statement:
A state $\omega$ on a $C^*$-algebra ${\mathcal B}$ is called a factor if the center of the von-Neumann algebra $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B})''$ is trivial, 
where $({\mathcal H}_{\omega},\pi_{\omega},\Omega)$ is the GNS space associated with $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ [BR vol-I].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
differentia: the center of the von-Neumann algebra $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B})''$ is trivial

nodes.name: Pure state
nodes.statement:
A state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ is called 
pure if $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B})''={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}_{\omega})$, the algebra of all bounded operators on ${\mathcal H}_{\omega}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: UHF algebra over the lattice Z^k
nodes.statement:
Let ${\mathcal B}=\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}^k} \!M_d(\mathbb{C})$ be the uniformly hyper-finite $C^*$-algebra over the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^k$ of dimension $k \ge 1$, where $\!M_d(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of $d \times d$-matrices 
over the field of complex number $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation invariant state
nodes.statement:
A state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ is called translation invariant if $\omega(x)=\omega(\theta_{\bar{m}}(x))$ where $\bar{m}=(m_1,m_2,.,m_k)$ and $\theta_{\bar{m}}$ 
is the translation induced by $\bar{\mathbb{Z}} \rightarrow  \bar{\mathbb{Z}} + \bar{m}$ for all $\bar{z} \in \mathbb{Z}^k$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Powers' criterion for translation invariant factor states
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: A translation invariant state is a factor state iff it has asymptotic clustering of correlations between far-away local algebras.
assumptions: a translation invariant state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$
conclusions: is a factor state if and only if

nodes.name: Quantum spin chain algebra B = tensor_Z M_d(C)
nodes.statement:
The quantum spin chain that
we consider here is described by a $\mbox{UHF}$ $C^*$-algebra denoted by ${\mathcal B}=\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M_d(\mathbb{C})$. Here ${\mathcal B}$
is the $C^*$ -completion of the infinite tensor product of the algebra $M_d(\mathbb{C})$ of $d \times d$ complex matrices [Sa],
each component of the tensor product element is indexed by an integer $j$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local element Q^(j)
nodes.statement:
We denote the element
$Q^{(j)}=...\otimes 1 \otimes 1 ... 1 \otimes Q \otimes 1 \otimes ... 1\otimes ,,. $, where $Q$
appears in the $j$-th component.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local subalgebra B_Lambda
nodes.statement:
Given a subset $\Lambda$ of $\mathbb{Z}$, ${\mathcal B}_{\Lambda}$ is defined as the $C^*$-sub-algebra
of ${\mathcal B}$ generated by all $Q^{(j)}$ with $Q \in {\bf M}_d(\mathbb{C})$, $j \in \Lambda$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Local algebra B_loc
nodes.statement:
We also set
$${\mathcal B}_{loc}= \bigcup_{\Lambda:|\Lambda| < \infty } {\mathcal B}_{\Lambda}$$
where $|\Lambda|$ is the cardinality of $\Lambda$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Restrictions omega_R and omega_L
nodes.statement:
We also set $\omega_{R}=\omega_{[1,\infty)}$ and $\omega_{L}=
\omega_{(-\infty,0]}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation automorphism theta_k
nodes.statement: The translation $\theta_k$ is an automorphism of ${\mathcal B}$ defined by $\theta_k(Q^{(j)})=Q^{(j+k)}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Translation invariant finite range Hamiltonian
nodes.statement:
We will consider a Hamiltonian in one dimensional lattice of the following form
\begin{equation} 
H= \sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} \theta^k(h_0)
\end{equation} 
for $h^*_0=h_0 \in {\mathcal B}_{loc}$ 
where the formal sum gives an auto-morphism $\alpha=(\alpha_t:t \in \mathbb{R})$ via the thermodynamic limit 
of $\alpha^{\Lambda}_t(x)=e^{itH_{\Lambda}}xe^{-itH_{\Lambda}}$ for a net of finite subsets of the lattice 
$\Lambda \uparrow \mathbb{Z}$ whose surface energies are uniformly bounded, where $H_{\Lambda}=\sum_{k \in \Lambda} \theta^k(h_0)$ [Ru,BR2].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Formal translation-invariant Hamiltonian H = sum of translates of a local h_0, generating dynamics by thermodynamic limit.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of KMS states for finite range interactions (Araki)
nodes.statement:
In such a case, i.e. translation invariant Hamiltonian $H$ having  
finite range interaction,  KMS state at a given inverse temperature exists and is unique [Ara1],[Ara2], [Ki] and inherits translation and other symmetry 
of the Hamiltonian.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: translation invariant Hamiltonian $H$ having finite range interaction
conclusions: KMS state at a given inverse temperature exists and is unique

nodes.name: Cuntz algebra O_d
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
differentia: generated by the elements $\{s_1,s_2,..., s_d \}$ subject to the following Cuntz relations:

nodes.name: Canonical U(d) action beta_g on O_d
nodes.statement:
There is a canonical action of the group $U(d)$ of unitary $d \times d$ matrices on ${\mathcal O}_d$ given by
$$\beta_g(s_i)=\sum_{1 \le j \le d}\overline{g^j_i}s_j$$
for $g=(g^i_j) \in U(d)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Gauge action beta_z
nodes.statement:
In particular the gauge action is defined by
$$\beta_z(s_i)=zs_i,\;\;z \in I\!\!T =S^1= \{z \in \mathbb{C}: |z|=1 \}.$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant subalgebra UHF_d
nodes.statement:
If UHF$_d$ is the fixed point sub-algebra under the gauge action, then UHF$_d$ is the closure of the
linear span of all Wick ordered monomials of the form
$$s_{i_1}...s_{i_k}s^*_{j_k}...s^*_{j_1}$$
which is also isomorphic to the UHF$_d$ algebra
$${\mathcal B}_R =\otimes^{\infty}_1M_d(\mathbb{C})$$
so that the isomorphism carries the Wick ordered monomial above into the matrix element
$$e^{i_1}_{j_1}(1)\otimes e^{i_2}_{j_2}(2) \otimes....\otimes e^{i_k}_{j_k}(k) \otimes 1 \otimes 1 ....$$
and the restriction of $\beta_g$ to $UHF_d$ is then carried to action
$$Ad(g)\otimes Ad(g) \otimes Ad(g) \otimes ....$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: UHF_d is the gauge-fixed subalgebra of O_d, isomorphic to the one-sided chain B_R with beta_g acting as Ad(g) on each site.

nodes.name: Canonical endomorphism lambda
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Index set of finite sequences
nodes.statement:
${\mathcal I}$ be the set of finite sequences
$I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_m)$ where
$i_k \in \mathbb{Z}_d$ and $m \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Multi-index monomials s_I
nodes.statement:
We also include empty set $\emptyset \in {\mathcal I}$ and set $s_{\emptyset }=1=s^*_{\emptyset}$,
$s_{I}=s_{i_1}......s_{i_m} \in {\mathcal O}_d $ and $s^*_{I}=s^*_{i_m}...s^*_{i_1} \in {\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: The set K_omega of lambda-invariant extensions
nodes.statement:
Using weak$^*$ compactness of 
the convex set of states on a $C^*$-algebra, a standard averaging method ensures that the set 
$$K_{\omega}=\{ \psi \in {\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d): \psi \lambda= \psi,\; \psi_| \mbox{UHF}_d = \omega_R \}$$ 
is a non-empty compact subset of ${\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d)$, where ${\mathcal S}({\mathcal O}_d)$ is the weak$^*$ compact convex set of states on ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: K_omega is the nonempty compact set of lambda-invariant states on O_d restricting to omega_R on UHF_d.

nodes.name: Support projection P of psi
nodes.statement:
We set 
$P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ to be the support projection of $\psi$ i.e. $P=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Support projection is sub-harmonic
nodes.statement:
Invariance property of the state $\psi=\psi \lambda$ will ensure that $P\Lambda(I-P)P=0$ where 
$$\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$$ 
is the canonical endomorphism on $\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ with $S_i=\pi_{\psi}(s_i)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: Invariance property of the state $\psi=\psi \lambda$

nodes.name: Popescu elements v_i = P S_i P and algebra M
nodes.statement:
We define a family of contractions $\{v_i:1 \le i \le d\}$ in ${\mathcal M}$ by 
$v_i=PS_iP,1 \le i \le d $ where we set von-Neumann algebra 
${\mathcal M}=P\pi_{\phi}({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ acting on Hilbert subspace ${\mathcal K}$ where ${\mathcal K}$ is range of $P$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Markov map tau
nodes.statement:
Thus we get ${\mathcal M} = \{v_i: 1 \le i \le d \}''$ 
and a unital completely positive map $\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P=\sum_iv_ixv_i^*$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Fixed points of tau are the commutant
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: the support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ being equal to $P$

nodes.name: Popescu's elements
nodes.statement:
A family of contractions $\{v_i:1 \le i \le d \}$ in ${\mathcal M}$ is called 
Popescu's elements if $\sum_iv_iv_i^*=1$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: State psi on O_d from a Popescu system
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: omega_R expressed by Popescu elements
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Completely positive map E on M_d(M)
nodes.statement:
We define
$$I\!\!E: \!M_d({\mathcal M}) \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$$ 
by 
$$I\!\!E(X)=VXV^*=\sum_{1 \le i,j \le d} v_ix^i_jv_j^* $$ 
where $X=((x^i_j))$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Quantum Markov representation of a translation invariant state
nodes.statement:
Let $\phi$ be a state on ${\mathcal M}$ such that 
$$\phi(I\!\!E(B \otimes I_d))=\phi(B),\;\forall B \in {\mathcal M} $$ For each $A \in M_d(\mathbb{C})$, define  
$I\!\!E_{A}:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$ 
by $$B \rightarrow I\!\!E(B \otimes A)$$ Then 
\begin{equation} 
\omega(A_1 \otimes A_1 \otimes A_3 ...\otimes A_m)=\phi(I\!\!E_{A_1} \circ I\!\!E_{A_2} \circ ..I\!\!E_{A_m}(I_{{\mathcal K}}))
\end{equation}
defines a $\lambda$-invariant state on ${\mathcal B}_R$ and the inductive limit state of ${\mathcal B}_R \rightarrow ^{\lambda} {\mathcal B}_R$ [Sa] 
gives a translation invariant state on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: An E-invariant state phi and maps E_A define a lambda-invariant state on B_R by phi(E_{A_1}...E_{A_m}(I)), extending to a translation invariant state on B.

nodes.name: Existence of the dual Markov map tilde tau
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: The state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x \Omega>$ on ${\mathcal M}$ being faithful and invariant of $\tau:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal M}$
conclusions: we find a unique unital completely positive map $\tilde{\tau}:{\mathcal M}' \rightarrow {\mathcal M}'$ satisfying the duality relation

nodes.name: Tomita conjugation J and modular operator Delta
nodes.statement:
$\phi$ being also a faithful state, $\Omega \in {\mathcal K}$ is a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$ and 
the closure of the close-able operator $S_0:x\Omega \rightarrow x^*\Omega, S$ possesses a polar decomposition
$S={\mathcal J} \Delta^{1/2}$, where ${\mathcal J}$ is an anti-unitary and $\Delta$ is a non-negative self-adjoint operator 
on ${\mathcal K}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Tomita's theorem
nodes.statement:
Tomita's [BR] theorem says that 
$\Delta^{it} {\mathcal M} \Delta^{-it}={\mathcal M},\;t \in \mathbb{R}$ and ${\mathcal J} {\mathcal M} {\mathcal J}={\mathcal M}'$, where ${\mathcal M}'$ is the
commutant of ${\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Modular automorphism group sigma_t
nodes.statement:
We define the modular automorphism group
$\sigma=(\sigma_t,\;t \in I\!\!T )$ on ${\mathcal M}$
by
$$\sigma_t(x)=\Delta^{it}x\Delta^{-it}$$ which satisfies the modular relation
$$\phi(x\sigma_{-{i \over 2}}(y))=\phi(\sigma_{{i \over 2}}(y)x)$$
for any two analytic elements $x,y$ for the automorphism.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements tilde v_k
nodes.statement: We set $\tilde{v}_k = \overline{ {\mathcal J} \sigma_{i \over 2}(v^*_k) {\mathcal J} } \in {\mathcal M}'$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual Popescu elements satisfy Popescu relation and time reversal
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: tilde v_I^* Omega = v_{tilde I}^* Omega
nodes.statement:
Moreover $\tilde{v}^*_I\Omega = 
{\mathcal J} \sigma_{i \over 2}(v_{\tilde{I}})^*{\mathcal J}\Omega= {\mathcal J} \Delta^{1 \over 2}v_{\tilde{I}}\Omega
=v^*_{\tilde{I}}\Omega$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Dual algebra tilde M
nodes.statement:
We also set $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ to be the von-Neumann algebra generated by 
$\{\tilde{v}_k: 1 \le k \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: When are the fixed points of the dual map equal to M
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: One-one correspondence omega <-> P_e for factor states
nodes.statement:
However by Lemma 7.4 in [BJKW] for a factor state $\omega$, if we choose an extreme point $\psi \in K_{\omega}$, 
two such extreme points $\psi$ and $\psi'$ in $K_{\omega}$ are related by $\psi'=\phi \beta_z$ for some $z \in S^1$, ${\mathcal P}$ is uniquely determined modulo a unitary conjugation. In other words we find a 
one-one correspondence between 
\begin{equation}
\omega \Leftrightarrow \omega_R \Leftrightarrow K^e_{\omega} \Leftrightarrow {\mathcal P}_e 
\end{equation}  
modulo unitary conjugation where $K^e_{\omega}$ denotes the set of extreme points in $K_{\omega}$ and ${\mathcal P}_e$ the set of Popescu's elements associated with extreme points 
of $K_{\omega}$ on support projection of the state as described above.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: For a factor state, extreme points of K_omega give Popescu elements unique up to unitary conjugation, yielding a bijection omega <-> P_e.

nodes.name: M is a factor and (M,tau,phi) is ergodic
nodes.statement:
Further in such a case ${\mathcal M}=\{v_k:1 \le k \le d\}''$ 
is a factor and $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is an ergodic {\it quantum dynamical system } [La,Ev].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Ergodic quantum dynamical system
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.genus: unital completely positive map $\tau$ on a von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}$ with an invariant normal state $\phi$

nodes.name: Haag duality
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality implies purity
nodes.statement: It is clear that such a factor state is pure.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: such a factor state

nodes.name: Haag duality for translation invariant pure states
nodes.statement:
A pure mathematical question that arises here whether converse is true? i.e. 
Do we always have Haag duality property for a translation invariant pure state of ${\mathcal B}$?
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Haag duality for type-I restrictions
nodes.statement:
In case $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor state, Haag duality property follows easily. In fact we can find Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi},\;{\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}$ such that
${\mathcal H}_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \otimes {\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^+_{\pi}}$
and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}} \otimes {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^+_{\pi})$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor state

nodes.name: Proof that type-I restriction gives Haag duality
nodes.statement:
A simple proof goes as follows: $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ being a type-I factor, its commutant 
is also a type-I factor. Thus we have an inclusion of type-I sub-factor $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$. Without loss of generality we assume now that
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$. Now we again 
use type-I factor property of $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$ to write ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \equiv {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1) \otimes {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)$ 
for two Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(k),\; k=1,2$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1)) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)}$. Since $\omega$ is pure we have 
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \bigcap \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'=\mathbb{C}$ and so ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)=\mathbb{C}$. Thus we arrive at 
our conclusion.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Type-I factor decomposition: write the commutant as B(H^-), split off pi(B_L)'' as a tensor factor, and use purity to kill the remaining factor.

nodes.name: Quantum Markov state (Accardi)
nodes.statement:
Functional relation (9) is called 
{\it quantum Marvov state } by Luigi Accardi [Ac] as a generalization of classical Markov state or more generally of a classical Gibbs state.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Finitely correlated state
nodes.statement:
When ${\mathcal M}$ is a matrix algebra in relations (9), it is called {\it finitely correlated state } and the general mathematical 
structures of such a translation invariant states on ${\mathcal B}$ were further investigated in details in [FNW2] [FNW3], [Ma1],[Ma2],[Ma3] and there afterward in [BJ] and [BJKW] for more general translation invariant states on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Trivial K gives a pure product state
nodes.statement:
If ${\mathcal K}=\mathbb{C}$, then 
Popescu elements are just some complex numbers i.e. $v_k=\lambda_k$, then $\omega$ is a pure tensor product state.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: ${\mathcal K}=\mathbb{C}$
conclusions: $\omega$ is a pure tensor product state

nodes.name: Bernoulli state
nodes.statement: We call such a state a {\it Bernoulli state}.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Projections e_n
nodes.statement:
Given a translation invariant state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, we set increasing sequence of projections $e_n=[\pi(\theta^n({\mathcal B}_R))'\Omega],\;n \in \mathbb{Z}$ in the GNS space 
$({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ associated with state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Mackey's imprimitivity criterion for the shift
nodes.statement:
The family of operators $(S_n,e_n-|\Omega><\Omega|)$ gives rise to a system of imprimitivity if and only if 
$e_{n} \downarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ as $n \downarrow -\infty$ [Mac].
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
conclusions: gives rise to a system of imprimitivity if and only if $e_{n} \downarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ as $n \downarrow -\infty$

nodes.name: Kolmogorov property
nodes.statement: We say $\omega$ admits Kolmogorov property if $e_n \downarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ as $n \downarrow -\infty$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Kolmogorov property implies purity
nodes.statement:
In particular Kolmogorov property
implies purity of $\omega$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: Kolmogorov property

nodes.name: Type-I or type-III dichotomy for translation invariant pure states (Mohari)
nodes.statement:
In [Mo4] we have shown that a translation invariant pure state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$ can give only type-I or type-III
factor states once we restrict to ${\mathcal B}_R$ (Theorem 3.4 in [Mo4] ).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.origin_citation: Mohari, Pure inductive limit state and Kolmogorov's property-II (Theorem 3.4)
assumptions: a translation invariant pure state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$
conclusions: can give only type-I or type-III factor states once we restrict to ${\mathcal B}_R$

nodes.name: Translation invariant pure states on B_R are product states (BJP)
nodes.statement: One interesting result in [BJP] says that any translation invariant pure state on ${\mathcal B}_R$ is also a product state and the canonical endomorphism associated with two such states are unitary equivalent.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: any translation invariant pure state on ${\mathcal B}_R$

nodes.name: Is mean entropy an invariant of translation dynamics
nodes.statement: In this context one interesting problem that remain open is whether mean entropy [Ru] is an invariance for translation dynamics.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Purity criterion via Popescu elements (Mohari, Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3])
nodes.statement:
Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3] gives a precise answer: $\omega$ is pure if and only if there exists a sequence of positive contractive elements $x_n \in {\mathcal M}$ such that 
$$x_n \rightarrow I,\;\;x_{m+n}\tau_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)I$$ 
in strong operator topology for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $m \ge 1$.

nodes.name: Gap in Theorem 7.1 of BJKW
nodes.statement: This statement can be taken as the correct version of Theorem 7.1 of [BJKW]. Theorem 7.1 in [BJKW] has aimed towards a sufficient condition on Popescu elements ${\mathcal P}$ for purity of the translation invariant state. However the statement and its proof are faulty as certain argument used in the proof is not time reversal symmetric and a factor state with Popescu elements on support projection satisfies the conditions of the statement of Theorem 7.1. One natural remedy to add additional hypothesis that (e) holds. In particular Lemma 7.6 in [BJKW] needs that additional assumption related to the support projection of the dual state $\tilde{\psi} \in K_{\tilde{\omega}}$. Besides this additional structure proof of Lemma 7.8 in [BJKW] is also not complete unless we find a proof for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ ( we retained same notations here in the text) for such a factor state $\omega$. Such a problem could have been solved if there were any method which shows directly that Takesaki's conditional [Ta] expectation exists from ${\mathcal M}'$ onto $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The purity criterion of BJKW Theorem 7.1 is faulty; it needs the extra support-projection hypothesis (e) and a proof that tilde M = M'.

nodes.name: Normal conditional expectation
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.genus: normal unital completely positive map $E_c:{\mathcal M} \rightarrow {\mathcal N}$

nodes.name: Takesaki's theorem on conditional expectations
nodes.statement:
A theorem of Takesaki's [Ta, also see AcC] says that conditional expectation $E_c$ preserving a faithful normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ exists if and only if the modular group $\sigma=(\sigma_t:t \in \mathbb{R})$ 
associated with $\phi$, which preserves ${\mathcal M}$, also preserves ${\mathcal N}$, i.e. $\sigma_t(x) \in {\mathcal N}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $x \in {\mathcal N}$.

conclusions: conditional expectation $E_c$ preserving a faithful normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ exists if and only if the modular group

nodes.name: Dual Stinespring representation of tilde O_d
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi:\tilde{{\mathcal O}_d} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}})$ be the minimal Stinespring representation so that 
$P\pi(\tilde{s}_I\tilde{s}_J^*)P=\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}_J^*$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty $.

nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Support projections e_0 and tilde e_0
nodes.statement:
Let $e_0=[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'\Omega]$ and $\tilde{e}_0=[\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'\Omega]$ be the 
support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi({\mathcal B}_R)''$ and $\pi({\mathcal B}_L)''$ respectively.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Projection q_0 and subspace K_0
nodes.statement:
We set projection $q_0=e_0 \tilde{e}_0$ and take ${\mathcal K}_0$ to be the subspace of ${\mathcal H}$ 
determined by the projection $q_0$.

nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (equivalent characterizations of purity and Haag duality)
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: For a translation invariant factor state, purity is equivalent to Haag duality and to cyclicity/commutant conditions on the corner algebras and dual Popescu elements.
assumptions: $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$
$\psi$ be an extremal element in $K_{\omega}$

nodes.name: Remark 1.2 (gap in Keyl-Matsui-Schlingemann-Werner)
nodes.statement:
The paper ``On Haag Duality for Pure States of Quantum Spin Chain'' 
by authors: M. Keyl, Taku Matsui, D. Schlingemann, R. F. Werner, Rev. Math. Phys. 20:707-724,2008 has an incomplete proof for Haag duality property as Lemma 4.3 in that paper has a faulty argument.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction

nodes.name: Theorem 2.1 (Popescu dilation and commutant lifting theorem)
nodes.statement:
Let $v_1,v_2,...,v_d$ be a family of bounded operators on a Hilbert space
${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$. Then there exists a unique up to
isomorphism Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}$, a projection $P$ on ${\mathcal K}$ and a family of isometries
$\{S_k:,\;1 \le k \le d \}$ satisfying Cuntz's relation so that
\begin{equation}
PS^{*}_{k}P=S_k^*P=v^*_k
\end{equation}
for all $1 \le k \le d$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation i.e. the vectors
$\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$.

Moreover the following holds:

\noindent (a) $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ where $\Lambda(X)=\sum_k S_kXS_k^*$;

\noindent (b) For any $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kxv_k^*=x \}$, 
$\Lambda^n(D) \rightarrow X'$ weakly as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for some $X'$ in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Moreover
the self adjoint elements in the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$ is isometrically
order isomorphic with the self adjoint elements in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ via the
surjective map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$, where ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_{1 \le k \le d }
v_kxv^*_k=x \}.$

\noindent (c) $\{v_k,v^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}' \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and equality holds if and only if
$P \in \{S_k,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$.

\vskip 1em 
If $(w_i)$ be another such an Popescu elements on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}'$ such that there exists an operator 
$u:{\mathcal K} \rightarrow {\mathcal K}'$ so that $\sum_k w_kuv_k^*=u$ then there exists an operator $U:{\mathcal H}_v \rightarrow {\mathcal H}_w$ so 
that $\pi'(x)U=U\pi(x)$ where $({\mathcal H}_w,\pi',S'_i)$ are Popescu dilation of $(w_i)$ and $\pi'$ is the associated
minimal representation of ${\mathcal O}_d$. In particular $U$ is isometry, unitary if $u$ is so respectively. If $u$ is unitary 
and ${\mathcal K}={\mathcal K}'$ then we can as well take ${\mathcal H}_v={\mathcal H}_w$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Popescu elements dilate uniquely to Cuntz isometries with P S_k^* P = v_k^*; commutant of the dilation is order-isomorphic to tau-fixed points.
assumptions: Let $v_1,v_2,...,v_d$ be a family of bounded operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$.
conclusions: there exists a unique up to isomorphism Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}$, a projection $P$ on ${\mathcal K}$ and a family of isometries

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement:
Following Popescu [Po] we define a completely positive map
$R: {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ by
\begin{equation}
R(s_Is^*_J)=v_Iv^*_J
\end{equation}
for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$. The representation $S_1,..,S_d$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$ on ${\mathcal H}$ thus may be taken to be the Stinespring
dilation of $R$ [BR, vol-2] and uniqueness up to unitary equivalence follows from uniqueness of the Stinespring
representation. That ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation follows from the minimality property of the Stinespring
dilation. 

\vskip 1em 
For (a) let $Q$ be the limiting projection of $\Lambda^n(P)$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Then we have $\Lambda(Q)=Q$ i.e. $Q\Lambda(I-Q)Q=0$ 
and so $(I-Q)S_k^*Q=0$. Interchanging the role of $Q$ with $I-Q$, we get $QS_k^*(I-Q)=0$. This shows $QS_k^*=S_k^*Q$ for all $1 le k \le d$. 
Since $Q$ is a projection, taking adjoint in the relation, we get $Q \in \{S_k,S^*_k\}'$. That $Q \ge P$ is obvious since $\Lambda^n(P) \ge P$ 
for all $n \ge 1$. In particular $QS_If=S_If$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and $|I| < \infty$. Hence $Q=I$ by the
cyclicity of ${\mathcal K}$. 

\vskip 1em 
For (b) essentially we deffer from the argument used in Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW]. We fix any $D
\in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and note that $P\Lambda_k(D)P=\tau_k(D)=D$ for any $k \ge 1$. Thus for any integers $n > m$
we have
$$\Lambda_m(P)\Lambda_n(D)\Lambda_m(P)=\Lambda_m(P\Lambda_{n-m}(D)P)=\Lambda_m(D)$$
Hence for any fixed $m \ge 1$ limit $<f,\Lambda_n(D)g>$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ exists for all
$f,g \in \Lambda_m(P)$. Since the family of operators $\Lambda_n(D)$ is uniformly bounded and $\Lambda_m(P) \uparrow I$
as $m \rightarrow \infty$, a standard density argument guarantees that the weak operator limit of $\Lambda_n(D)$ exists as
$n \rightarrow \infty$. Let $X'$ be the limit. So $\Lambda(X')=X'$, by Cuntz's relation, $X' \in \{S_k,S^*_k:1 \le k \le k \}'$.
Since $P\Lambda_n(D)P=D$ for all $n \ge 1$, we also conclude that $PX'P=D$ by taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$. Conversely,
it is obvious that $P\{ S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Hence
we can identify $P\{S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P$ with ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.

\vskip 1em
Further it is obvious that $X'$ is self-adjoint if and only if $D=PX'P$ is self-adjoint ( since $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, 
by taking limit $\Lambda^n(PXP)=\Lambda^n(PX^*P)$ shows that $X^*=X$ if $D^*=D$ ). Now fix any self-adjoint element $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Since 
the identity operator on ${\mathcal K}$ is an element in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ for any $\alpha \ge 0$ for which $- \alpha P  \le D \le \alpha P$, we have $\alpha 
\Lambda_n(P) \le \Lambda_n(D) \le \alpha \Lambda_n(P)$ for all $n \ge 1$. By taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$ we
conclude that $- \alpha I \le X' \le \alpha I$, where $PX'P=D$. Since operator norm of a self-adjoint element $A$
in a Hilbert space is given by
$$||A||= \mbox{inf}_{\alpha \ge 0}\{\alpha: - \alpha I  \le A \le \alpha I \}$$
we conclude that $||X'|| \le ||D||$. That $||D||=||PX'P|| \le ||X'||$ is obvious, $P$ being a
projection. Thus the map is isometrically order isomorphic taking self-adjoint elements of the commutant
to self-adjoint elements of ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.

\vskip 1em
We are left to prove (c). Inclusion is trivial. For the last part, we assume first that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For any element $D$
in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d\}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Since $P$ commutes with $X'$, 
we verify that 
$$Dv^*_k= PX'PS^*_kP=PX'S^*_kP=PS^*_kX'P=PS^*_kPX'P=v^*_kD$$ 
We also have $D^* \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and thus $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Hence $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$. Since $P\pi_{\hat{\omega}}
({\mathcal O}_d)'P = {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. Thus equality holds whenever
$P \in \{S_k,S_k^*,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$. 

\vskip 1em 
For the converse note that by commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements
of the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$.
Hence $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW]. 

\vskip 1em 
For the proof of intertwining relation and their property we refer to main body of the proof of 
Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Stinespring dilation of the Popescu cp map; limits of Lambda^n give the commutant lifting and isometric order isomorphism.

nodes.name: Popescu's dilation
nodes.statement:
A family $(v_k,1 \le k \le d)$ of contractive operators on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ is called Popescu's elements if $\sum_kv_kv_k^*=I$ 
and the dilation $({\mathcal H},P,{\mathcal K},S_k,1 \le k \le d)$ in Theorem 2.1 is called Popescu's dilation to Cuntz elements.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2 (states on O_d and Popescu systems)
nodes.statement:
There exists a canonical one-one correspondence between the following objects:

\vskip 1em
\noindent (a) States $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$

\vskip 1em
\noindent (b) Function $C: {\mathcal I} \times {\mathcal I} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with the following properties:

\noindent (i) $C(\emptyset, \emptyset)=1$;

\noindent (ii) for any function $\lambda:{\mathcal I} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ with finite support we have
         $$\sum_{I,J \in {\mathcal I}} \overline{\lambda(I)}C(I,J)\lambda(J) \ge 0$$

\noindent (iii) $\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_d} C(Ii,Ji) = C(I,J)$ for all $I,J \in {\mathcal I}$.

\vskip 1em
\noindent (c) Unitary equivalence class of objects $({\mathcal K},\Omega,v_1,..,v_d)$ where

\noindent (i) ${\mathcal K}$ is a Hilbert space and $\Omega$ is a unit vector in ${\mathcal K}$;

\noindent (ii) $v_1,..,v_d \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_d} v_iv^*_i=1$;

\noindent (iii) the linear span of the vectors of the form $v^*_I\Omega$, where $I \in {\mathcal I}$, is dense in ${\mathcal K}$.

\vskip 1em
The correspondence is given by a unique completely positive map $R: {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$, where 

\noindent (i) $R(s_Is^*_J)=v_Iv^*_J;$

\noindent (ii) $\psi(x)=<\Omega,R(x)\Omega>;$

\noindent (iii) $\psi(s_Is^*_J)=C(I,J)=<v^*_I \Omega,v^*_J\Omega>;$

\noindent (iv) For any fixed $g \in U_d$, the completely positive map $R_g:{\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ defined by $R_g= R
\circ \beta_g$ give rises to a Popescu system given by $({\mathcal K},\Omega,\beta_g(v_i),..,\beta_g(v_d))$ where
$\beta_g(v_i)=\sum_{1 \le j \le d} \overline{g^i_j} v_j.$
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: States on O_d correspond bijectively to positive-definite kernels C(I,J) and to cyclic Popescu systems (K,Omega,v_i).
conclusions: There exists a canonical one-one correspondence between the following objects:

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: For a proof we simply refer to Proposition 2.1 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: By citation of Proposition 2.1 in BJKW.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.3 (minimal Popescu elements of a state on O_d)
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi$ be a state on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ be the GNS space associated with 
$({\mathcal O}_d,\psi)$. We set $S_i=\pi(s_i)$ and normal state $\psi_{\Omega}$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ defined by 
$$\psi_{\Omega}(X) = <\Omega, X \Omega>$$
Let $P$ be the projection on the closed subspace ${\mathcal K}$ generated by the vectors $\{S^*_I\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$ and 
\begin{equation}
v_k=PS_kP
\end{equation}
for $1 \le k \le d$. Then following holds:

\vskip 1em
\noindent (a) $\{v^*_I\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$ is total in ${\mathcal K}$.

\noindent (b) $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$;

\noindent (c) $S_k^*P=PS_k^*P$ for all $1 \le k \le d$; 

\noindent (d) For any $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_k),J=(j_1,j_2,...,j_l)$ with $|I|,|J| < \infty$ we have 
\begin{equation} 
\psi(s_Is^*_J)= <\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>
\end{equation} 
and the vectors $\{ S_If: f \in {\mathcal K},\;|I| < \infty \}$ are total in
the GNS Hilbert space associated with $({\mathcal O}_d,\psi)$. Further such a family $({\mathcal K},\;v_k,\;1 \le k \le d,\;\omega)$ satisfying
(a) to (d) is determined uniquely up to isomorphism. 

\vskip 1em
Conversely given a Popescu system $({\mathcal K},v_k,\;1 \le k \le d,\Omega)$ satisfying (a) and (b) there exists a unique   state 
$\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ so that (c) and (d) are satisfied.

Furthermore the following statements are valid:
\vskip 1em
\noindent (e)  If the normal state $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x \Omega>$ on the von-Neumann algebra
${\mathcal M}=\{ v_i, v^*_i \}''$ is invariant for the Markov map $\tau(x)=\sum_{1 \le k
\le d} v_ixv^*_i,\;x \in {\mathcal M}$ then $\psi$ is $\lambda$ invariant and $\phi$ is faithful 
on ${\mathcal M}$.

\vskip 1em
\noindent (f) If $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ then following are equivalent:

\noindent (i) $\psi$ is an ergodic state for $({\mathcal O}_d,\lambda)$; 

\noindent (ii) $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic;

\noindent (ii) ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The cyclic subspace of S_I^* Omega gives Popescu elements v_k=PS_kP representing psi; invariance of phi gives lambda-invariance and faithfulness.
assumptions: Let $\psi$ be a state on ${\mathcal O}_d$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement:
We fix a state $\psi$ and consider the GNS space  $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$
associated with $({\mathcal O}_d,\psi)$ and set $S_i=\pi(s_i)$. It is obvious 
that $S^*_kP \subseteq P$ for all $1 \le k \le d $, thus $P$ is the minimal subspace 
containing $\Omega$ and invariant by all $\{ S^*_k;\;1 \le k \le d \}$ i.e.
\begin{equation}
PS^*_kP=S^*_kP
\end{equation}
Thus $v^*_k=PS^*_kP=S_k^*P$ and so $\sum_k v_kv^*_k = \sum_k PS_kS^*_kP= P$ which is 
identity operator in ${\mathcal K}$. This completes the proof of (a) (b) and (c).

\vskip 1em
For (d) we note that
$$\psi(s_Is^*_J)$$
$$=<\Omega, S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$
$$=<\Omega,PS_IS^*_JP\Omega>$$
$$=<\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>.$$
Since ${\mathcal H}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega:|I|,|J| < \infty \}$ and
${\mathcal K}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{ S^*_J\Omega=v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$, 
${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for $S_I$ i.e. the vectors $\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ spans 
${\mathcal H}$. Uniqueness up to isomorphism follows as usual by total property of vectors 
$v^*_I\Omega$ in ${\mathcal K}$. 

\vskip 1em
Conversely for a Popescu's elements $({\mathcal K},v_i,\Omega)$ satisfying (a) and (b), we consider
the family $({\mathcal H},S_k,\;1 \le k \le d,P)$ of Cuntz's elements defined as in
Theorem 2.1. We claim that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow
S_i$. Note that by our construction vectors $\{S_If,f \in {\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total
in ${\mathcal H}$ and $v^*_J\Omega=S^*_J\Omega$ for all $|J| < \infty$. Thus by our hypothesis that
vectors $\{v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal K}$, we verify that
vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$. Hence $\Omega$ is a cyclic for
the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$.

\vskip 1em
We are left to prove (e) and (f). It simple to note by (d) that $\psi \lambda=\psi$ i.e.
$$\sum_i <\Omega,S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_i\Omega>= \sum_i <\Omega,v_iv_Iv^*_Jv^*_i\Omega> $$
$$=<\Omega,v_Iv_J^*\Omega> = <\Omega,S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ where 
in the second equality we have used our hypothesis that the vector state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ 
is $\tau$-invariant. In such case we aim now to show that $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. To that end 
let $p'$ be the support projection in ${\mathcal M}$ for $\tau$ invariant state $\phi$. Thus $\phi(1-p') = 0$ 
i.e. $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and by invariance we also have $\phi(p'\tau(1-p')p')=\phi(1-p')=0$. Since $p'\tau(1-p')p' \ge 0 $ and an element in 
${\mathcal M}$, by minimality of support projection, we 
conclude that $p'\tau(1-p')p'=0$. Hence $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and $p'v^*_kp'=v^*_kp'$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. 
Thus $p'v^*_I\Omega=v^*_I\Omega$ for all 
$|I| < \infty$. As ${\mathcal K}$ is the closed linear span of the vectors $\{ v_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$, we conclude 
that $p'=p$. In other words $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. This completes the proof for (e).

\vskip 1em
We are left to show (f) where we assume that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, the weak$^*$ limit of the increasing 
projection $\Lambda^k(P)$ is $I$. Thus by Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] we have $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic if and only if the reduced dynamics 
$({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic. For the last part of the statement, we need to show for a projection $e \in {\mathcal M}$, $\tau(e)=e$ if and only if $e \in {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$.
It is an easy consequence since $\tau(e)=e$ says that $e\tau(I-e)e=0$ and so $(1-e)v_k^*e=0$. Changing the role of $e$ by $I-e$, we also get $ev_k^*(I-e)=0$ for
all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus we get that $e$ commutes with each $v_k$. $P$ being in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $v_k \in {\mathcal M}$. So $e \in {\mathcal M}'$. Thus by a standard theorem [La,Ev,Fr,BJKW] 
ergodic property is equivalent to factor property of ${\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Direct verification from GNS construction and Theorem 2.1; faithfulness via support projection argument; ergodicity via Mohari's reduced dynamics result.

nodes.name: Unique KMS state of the gauge-type flow on O_d
nodes.statement:
Before we move to our next result, we comment here that in general for a $\lambda$ invariant state on ${\mathcal O}_d$, 
the normal state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}=\{v_k,v_k^*:1 \le k \le d \}''$ need not be invariant for $\tau$. To that 
end we consider ( [BR] vol-II page 110 ) the unique KMS state $\psi=\psi_{\beta}$ for the automorphism $\alpha_t(s_i)=e^{it}s_i$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$. $\psi$ is $\lambda$ 
invariant and $\psi_{|\mbox{UHF}_d}$ is the unique faithful trace. $\psi$ being a KMS state for an automorphism, the normal state induced by the cyclic vector on 
$\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ is also separating for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. As $\psi \beta_z = \psi$ for all $z \in S^1$ we have 
$<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>=<\Omega,\beta_z(s_I)\Omega> = z^{|I|}<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>$ for all $z \in S^1$ and 
so $<\Omega,\pi(s_I)\Omega>=0$ for all $|I| \ge 1$. In particular $<\Omega,v_I^*\Omega>=0$ where $(v_i)$ are defined 
as in Proposition 2.3 and thus $<v_i\Omega,v^*_I\Omega>=<\Omega,v^*_iv_I\Omega>=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $v_i\Omega=0$. By Proposition 2.3 (e), $\Omega$ is 
separating for ${\mathcal M}$ and so we get $v_i=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$ and this contradicts that $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=1$. Thus we conclude by Proposition 2.3 (e) that 
$\phi$ is not $\tau$ invariant on ${\mathcal M}$. This example also indicates that the support projection of a $\lambda$ invariant state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ need 
not be equal to the minimal sub-harmonic projection $P$ i.e. the closed span of vectors $\{ S_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$ containing $\Omega$ and $\{v_Iv_J^*: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ 
need not be even an algebra.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: For the unique KMS state of alpha_t(s_i)=e^{it}s_i, the vector state on M is not tau-invariant and the minimal sub-harmonic projection is not the support projection.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.4 (Popescu elements on the support projection)
nodes.statement:
Let $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$ be the GNS representation of a $\lambda$ invariant state 
$\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $P$ be the support projection of the normal state $\psi_{\Omega}(X)=<\Omega,X\Omega>$ in the 
von-Neumann algebra $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Then the following holds:

\vskip 1em
\noindent (a) $P$ is a sub-harmonic projection for the endomorphism $\Lambda(X)=\sum_k S_kXS^*_k$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$
i.e. $\Lambda(P) \ge P$ satisfying the following:

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (i) $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$;

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (ii) $PS^*_kP=S^*_kP,\;\;1 \le k \le d$;

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (iii) $\sum_{1 \le k \le d} v_kv_k^*=I$ 

where $S_k=\pi(s_k)$ and $v_k=PS_kP$ for $1 \le k \le d$;

\vskip 1em
\noindent (b) For any $I=(i_1,i_2,...,i_k),J=(j_1,j_2,...,j_l)$ with $|I|,|J| < \infty$ we have $\psi(s_Is^*_J) =
<\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>$ and the vectors $\{ S_If: f \in {\mathcal K},\;|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$;

\vskip 1em
\noindent (c) The von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}=P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P$, acting on the Hilbert space
${\mathcal K}$ i.e. the range of $P$, is generated by $\{v_k,v^*_k:1 \le k \le d \}''$ and the normal state
$\phi(x)=<\Omega,x \Omega>$ is faithful on the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}$.

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (d) The self-adjoint part of the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ is norm and order isomorphic to the space
of self-adjoint fixed points of the completely positive map $\tau$. The isomorphism takes $X' \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$
onto $PX'P \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$, where ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K}) = \{ x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x \}$ and 
$\tau(x)=\sum_kv_kxv^*_k,\;x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. Furthermore ${\mathcal M}' = {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.

\vskip 1em
Conversely let ${\mathcal M}$ be a von-Neumann algebra generated by a family $\{v_k: 1 \le k \le d \}$ of bounded operators
on a Hilbert space ${\mathcal K}$ so that $\sum_kv_kv_k^*=1$ and the commutant 
\begin{equation} 
{\mathcal M}'=\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \sum_k v_kxv_k^*=x \}
\end{equation} 
Then the Popescu dilation $({\mathcal H},P,S_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ described in Theorem 2.1 satisfies the following:

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (i) $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$;

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (ii) For any faithful normal $\tau-$invariant state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ there exists a state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$ defined by
$$\psi(s_Is^*_J)=\phi(v_Iv^*_J),\;|I|,|J| < \infty $$
such that the GNS space associated with $({\mathcal M},\phi)$ is the support projection
for $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ satisfying (a)-(d). 

\vskip 1em
Further for a given $\lambda$-invariant state $\psi$, the family $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},v_k\;1 \le k \le d,\phi)$ satisfying (a)-(d) 
is determined uniquely up to unitary conjugation. 

\vskip 1em
\noindent (e) $\phi$ is a faithful normal $\tau$-invariant state on ${\mathcal M}$. Furthermore the following statements are equivalent:

\noindent (i) $({\mathcal O}_d,\lambda,\psi)$ is ergodic;

\noindent (ii) $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic;

\noindent (iii) ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: For a lambda-invariant state, the support projection P is sub-harmonic, phi is faithful on M=P pi(O_d)''P, and M' equals the tau-fixed points; ergodicity is equivalent to M being a factor.
assumptions: $\psi$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$
$P$ be the support projection of the normal state $\psi_{\Omega}(X)=<\Omega,X\Omega>$ in the von-Neumann algebra $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement:
$\Lambda(P)$ is also a projection in $\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''$ so that
$\psi_{\Omega}(\Lambda(P))=1$ by invariance property. Thus we have $\Lambda(P) \ge P$ i.e.
$P\Lambda(I-P)P=0$. Hence we have
\begin{equation}
PS^*_kP=S^*_kP
\end{equation}
Moreover by $\lambda$ invariance property we also note that the faithful normal state
$\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ on the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal M}=P\pi_{\psi}({\mathcal O}_d)''P$
is invariant for the reduced Markov map [Mo1] on ${\mathcal M}$ given by
\begin{equation}
\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P
\end{equation}
\vskip 1em
We claim that $\mbox{lim}_{n \uparrow \infty}\Lambda^n(P)= I$. That $\{ \Lambda^n(P): n \ge 1 \}$
is a sequence of increasing projections follows from sub-harmonic property of $P$ and endomorphism
property of $\Lambda$. Let the limiting projection be $Y$. Then $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ and so $Y \in
\{S_k,S^*_k \}'$. Since by our construction, the GNS Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\hat{\omega}}}$ is
generated by $S_IS^*_J\Omega$, $Y$ is a scalar. $Y$ being a non-zero projection, it is
the identity operator in ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\psi}}$.

\vskip 1em
Now it is routine to verify (a) (b) and (c). For the first part of (d) we appeal to Theorem 2.1. For the last part
note that for any invariant element $D$ in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ so that $PX'P=D$.
Since $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ we note that $(1-P)X'P=0$.
Now since $X' \in \{ S_k,S^*_k \}'$, we verify that $Dv^*_k= PXPS^*_kP=PXS^*_kP=PS^*_kXP=PS^*_kPXP=v^*_kD$. Since $D^* \in
{\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ we also have $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Thus $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'={\mathcal M}'$. Since
$P\pi_{\hat{\omega}}({\mathcal O}_d)'P=
{\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. The reverse inclusion is trivial.
This completes the proof for (d).

\vskip 1em
For the converse part: for (i), since by our assumption and the commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements of the commutant
$\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$,
$P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW]. For (ii) without loss of generality, we assume
that $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $\Omega$ is a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$.
( otherwise we set state $\psi(s_Is^*_J)=\phi(v_Iv_J^*)$ and consider its GNS representation )
We are left to show that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow S_i$. To that end 
let $Y \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ be the projection on the subspace generated by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega:  
|I|,|J| < \infty \}$. Note that, $P$ being an element in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $Y$ also commutes with all the elements of 
$P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P=P {\mathcal M} P$. Hence $Yx\Omega=x\Omega$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. Thus $Y \ge P$.  
Since $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ by our construction, we conclude that $Y=\Lambda_n(Y) 
\ge \Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Hence $Y=I$. In other words
$\Omega$ is cyclic for the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$. This completes the proof for (ii). 

\vskip 1em
Uniqueness up to unitary isomorphism follows as GNS representation is determined uniquely up to unitary conjugation 
and so its support projection.  

\vskip 1em
The first part of (e) we note that $PS_IS^*_JP=v_Iv_J^*$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ and thus ${\mathcal M}=P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ is the von-Neumann 
algebra generated by $\{v_k,v_k^*:1 \le k \le d \}$ and thus $\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. That $\phi$ is 
$\tau(x)=\sum_k v_kxv_k^*$ invariant follows as $\psi$ is $\lambda$-invariant. We are left to prove equivalence of statements (i)-(iii).  

\vskip 1em
By Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] the Markov semi-group $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic if and
only if $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic ( here we need to recall by (a) that
$\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). By a standard result [Ev, also BJKW] $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$
is ergodic if and only if there is no non trivial projection $e$ invariant for $\tau$ i.e. ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} = \{e \in {\mathcal M}: e^*=e,e^2=e,\tau(e)=e \}=\{0,1 \}$. 
If $\tau(e)=e$ for some projection $e \in {\mathcal M} $ then $(1-e)\tau(e)(1-e)=0$ and so $ev^*_k(1-e)=0$. Same is true 
if we replace $e$ by $1-e$ as $\tau(1-e)=\tau(1)-\tau(e)=1-e$ and so $(1-e)v^*_ke=0$. Thus $e$ commutes with $v_k,v_k^*$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. 
Hence ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$. Inequality in the reverse direction is trivial and thus ${\mathcal I}^{\tau}$ is trivial if and only if ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor. 
This shows equivalence of (ii) and (iii) follows by a standard result [La,Fr] in non-commutative ergodic theory. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Sub-harmonicity from invariance, Lambda^n(P) increases to I by cyclicity, and the commutant-lifting map of Theorem 2.1 identifies M' with tau-fixed points.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.5 (gauge symmetry group H of an extremal state)
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi$ be a $\lambda$ invariant factor state on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$
be its GNS representation. Then the following holds:

\noindent (a) The closed subgroup $H=\{z \in S^1: \psi \beta_z =\psi \}$ is equal to 

$$\{z \in S^1: \beta_z \mbox{extends to an automorphism of } \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \} $$ 

\noindent (b) Let ${\mathcal O}_d^{H}$ be the fixed point sub-algebra in ${\mathcal O}_d$ under the action of gauge group $\{ \beta_z: z \in H \}$. Then  
$\pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})'' = \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''$.

\noindent (c) If $H$ is a finite cyclic group of $k$ many elements and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor, 
then $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)' \equiv \mathbb{C}^m$ where $1 \le m \le k$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: For a lambda-invariant factor state, the gauge stabiliser H equals the set of extendable gauge automorphisms and H-fixed points generate the same von Neumann algebra as UHF_d.
assumptions: Let $\psi$ be a $\lambda$ invariant factor state on ${\mathcal O}_d$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement:
It is simple that $H$ is a closed subgroup. For any fix $z \in H $ we define unitary operator $U_z$ 
extending the map $\pi(x)\Omega \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))\Omega$ and check that the map $X \rightarrow U_zXU^*_z$ extends $\beta_z$ 
to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For the converse we will use the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a $\lambda$-invariant 
factor state and $\beta_z \lambda= \lambda \beta_z$ to guarantee that $\psi \beta_z (X) = {1 \over n} 
\sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \lambda^k \beta_z(X) = {1 \over n} \sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \beta_z \lambda^k(X) 
\rightarrow \psi(X)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for any $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, where we have used the same symbol $\beta_z$ 
for the extension. Hence $z \in H$. 

\vskip 1em
In the following instead of working with ${\mathcal O}_d$ we should be working with the inductive limit $C^*$ algebra and their inductive limit states. 
For simplicity of notation we still use $UHF_d,{\mathcal O}_d$ for its inductive limit of ${\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} {\mathcal O}_d$ 
and $UHF_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} UHF_d$ respectively and so for its inductive limit states.   

\vskip 1em
Now we aim to prove (b). $H$ being a closed subgroup of $S^1$, it is either entire $S^1$ or a finite subgroup 
$\{exp({ 2i \pi l \over k})|l=0,1,...,k-1 \}$ where the integer $k \ge 1$. If $H=S^1$ we have nothing to prove 
for (b). When $H$ is a finite closed subgroup, we identify $[0,1)$ with $S^1$ by the usual map and note that 
if $\beta_t$ is restricted to $t \in [0,{1 \over k})$, then by scaling we check that $\beta_t$ defines a 
representation of $S^1$ in automorphisms of ${\mathcal O}^H_d$. Now we consider the direct integral representation 
$\pi'$ defined by
$$\pi'= \int^{\oplus}_{[0,{1 \over k})} dt \pi_{|_{{\mathcal O}^H_d}} \beta_t $$
of ${\mathcal O}_d^{H}$ on ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}\otimes L^2([0,{1 \over k})\;)$, where ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}$ is the cyclic
space of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)$ generated by $\Omega$. That it is indeed direct integral follows as states
$\psi \beta_{t_1}$ and $\psi \beta_{t_2}$ are either same or orthogonal for a factor state $\psi$ (see the proof of Lemma 7.4 in [BJKW] for further details).
Interesting point here to note that the new representation $\pi'$ 
is $(\beta_t)$ co-variant i.e. $\pi' \beta_t=\beta_t \pi' $, hence by simplicity of the $C^*$ algebra ${\mathcal O}_d$ we 
conclude that $$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''^{\beta_t}$$
 
\vskip 1em
By exploring the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a factor state, 
we also have as in Lemma 6.11 in [BJKW] $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;) \subset \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''$. 
Hence we also have
$$\pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''= \pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)'' \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;).$$ 
Since $\beta_t$ is acting as translation on $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;)$ which being 
an ergodic action, we have 
$$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})'' \otimes 1$$
Since $\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' \otimes 1$, we conclude 
that $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''$. 

\vskip 1em
A proof for the statement (c) follows from Lemma 7.12 in [BJKW]. The original idea of the proof can be 
traced back to Arveson's work on spectrum of an automorphism of a commutative compact group [Ar1].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Averaging over lambda for (a); a direct integral over the gauge circle with ergodic translation action for (b); Lemma 7.12 of BJKW for (c).

nodes.name: lambda-invariant state omega' on UHF_d
nodes.statement: Let $\omega'$ be an $\lambda$-invariant state on the $\mbox{UHF}_d$ sub-algebra of ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem

nodes.name: The set K_omega' for a lambda-invariant state on UHF_d
nodes.statement:
Following [BJKW, section 7], 
we consider the set 
$$K_{\omega'}= \{ \psi: \psi \mbox{ is a state on } {\mathcal O}_d \mbox{ such that } \psi \lambda =
\psi \mbox{ and } \psi_{|\mbox{UHF}_d} = \omega' \}$$
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem

nodes.name: K_omega' is non-empty, convex and compact
nodes.statement:
By taking invariant mean on an extension of $\omega'$ to ${\mathcal O}_d$, we verify that $K_{\omega'}$ is non empty and 
$K_{\omega'}$ is clearly convex and compact in the weak topology.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem

nodes.name: K_omega' is a face for ergodic omega'
nodes.statement:
In case $\omega'$ is an ergodic state ( extremal state )
$K_{\omega'}$ is a face in the $\lambda$ invariant states.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
assumptions: $\omega'$ is an ergodic state ( extremal state )
conclusions: $K_{\omega'}$ is a face in the $\lambda$ invariant states

nodes.name: Proposition 2.6 (extreme points of K_omega', BJKW Lemma 7.4)
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega'$ be ergodic. Then $\psi \in K_{\omega'}$ is an extremal point in
$K_{\omega'}$ if and only if $\psi$ is a factor state and moreover any other extremal point in $K_{\omega'}$
has the form $\psi \beta_z$ for some $z \in S^1$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
assumptions: Let $\omega'$ be ergodic.
conclusions: $\psi \in K_{\omega'}$ is an extremal point in $K_{\omega'}$ if and only if $\psi$ is a factor state

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.6
nodes.statement:
Though Proposition 7.4 in [BJKW] appeared in a different set up, the same proof goes through for
the present case. We omit the details and refer to the original work for a proof.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Same proof as Proposition 7.4 of BJKW; details omitted.

nodes.name: Translation invariant state from a Popescu system
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be the translation invariant state on UHF$_d =\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}M_d$ defined by
$$\omega(e^{i_1}_{j_1}(l) \otimes e^{i_2}_{j_2}(l+1) \otimes ....\otimes e^{i_n}_{j_n}(l+n-1)) = \phi(v_Iv^*_J)$$
where $e^i_j(l)$ is the elementary matrix at lattice site $l \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Amalgamated tensor product H tensor_K tilde H
nodes.statement:
Following [BJKW] we consider the amalgamated tensor product ${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ of ${\mathcal H}$ with 
$\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ over the joint subspace ${\mathcal K}$. It is the completion of the quotient of the set $$\mathbb{C} \bar{I} \otimes 
\mathbb{C} I \otimes {\mathcal K},$$ where $\bar{I},I$ both consist of all finite sequences with elements in $\{1,2, ..,d \}$, 
by the equivalence relation defined by a semi-inner product defined on the set by requiring
$$<\bar{I} \otimes I \otimes f,\bar{I}\bar{J} \otimes IJ \otimes g>=<f,\tilde{v}_{\bar{J}}v_Jg>,$$
$$<\bar{I}\bar{J} \otimes I \otimes f, \bar{I} \otimes IJ \otimes g> =<\tilde{v}_{\bar{J}}f,v_Jg>$$
and all inner product that are not of these form are zero.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Completion of formal triples (bar I, I, f) modulo the semi-inner product built from tilde v and v, gluing the two Popescu dilations over K.

nodes.name: Commuting representations S_i and tilde S_i on the amalgamated space
nodes.statement:
We also define
two commuting representations $(S_i)$ and $(\tilde{S}_i)$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$ on
${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ by the following prescription:
$$S_I\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes J \otimes f)=\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes IJ \otimes f),$$
$$\tilde{S}_{\bar{I}}\lambda(\bar{J} \otimes J \otimes f)=\lambda(\bar{J}\bar{I} \otimes J \otimes f),$$
where $\lambda$ is the quotient map from the index set to the Hilbert space.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1 (amalgamated representation)
nodes.statement:
The following holds: 

\noindent (a) For any $1 \le i,j \le d$ and $|I|,|J|< \infty$ and $|\bar{I}|,|\bar{J}| < \infty$
$$<\Omega,\tilde{S}_{\bar{I}}\tilde{S}^*_{\bar{J}} S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_j \Omega>=<\Omega, 
\tilde{S}_i \tilde{S}_{\bar{I}}\tilde{S}^*_{\bar{J}}\tilde{S}^*_jS_IS^*_J \Omega>;$$

\noindent (b) The vector state $\psi_{\Omega}$ on $$\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d \equiv
\otimes_{-\infty}^0 M_d \otimes_1^{\infty}M_d \equiv \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} M_d$$ is equal to $\omega$;

\noindent (c) $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ if and only if
$\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x,\; \tilde{\tau}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in  \mathbb{C} \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: On the amalgamated space, the vector state is omega on the two-sided chain, and the representation is irreducible iff the common fixed points of tau and tilde tau are scalars.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement:
By our construction $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega =\tilde{v}^*_i\Omega=v_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$. Now (a) and (b) 
follow by repeated application of $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and
the commuting property of the two representation $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes I)$ and $\pi(I \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)$. The last
statement (c) follows from a more general fact proved below
that the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is
order isomorphic with the set $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x,\; \tilde{\tau}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in  \mathbb{C} \}$ via the 
map $X \rightarrow PXP$ where $X$ is the weak$^*$ limit of $\{\Lambda^m\tilde{\Lambda}^n(x)$ as $(m,n) \rightarrow 
(\infty,\infty)$. For details let $Y$ be the strong limit of increasing sequence of projections 
$(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^n(P)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j, S^*_i\tilde{S}^*_j$ 
for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. As $\Lambda(P)) \ge P$, we also have $\Lambda(Y) \ge Y$. Hence $(1-Y)S_i^*Y=0$. As $Y$ commutes 
with $S_i\tilde{S}_j$ we get $(1-Y)S_i^*S_i\tilde{S}_jY=0$ i.e. $(1-Y)\tilde{S}_jY=0$ for all $1 \le j \le d$. By symmetry 
of the argument we also get $(1-Y)S_iY=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $Y$ commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and by symmetry of 
the argument $Y$ commutes as well with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. As $Yf=f$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the 
representation $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$ we conclude that $Y=I$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$.

\vskip 1em
Let $x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\tau(x)=x$ and $\tilde{\tau}(x) = x $ then as in the proof of Theorem 2.1 
we also check that $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P) \Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) (\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P)$ is 
independent of $m,n$ as long as $m,n \ge k$. Hence the weak$^*$ limit $\Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) \rightarrow X$ exists 
as $m,n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore the limiting element $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$ and $PXP=x$. That the 
map $X \rightarrow PXP$ is an order-isomorphic on the set of self adjoint elements follows as in Theorem 2.1. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Use S_i^* Omega = tilde S_i^* Omega and commuting representations; for (c) lift common fixed points by joint limits of Lambda^m tilde Lambda^n as in Theorem 2.1.

nodes.name: Amalgamated space is the Popescu dilation of v_i tilde v_j
nodes.statement:
In short Proposition 3.1 also says that $(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H},S_i\tilde{S}_j\;1 \le i,j \le d,P)$ 
is the Popescu dilation associated with Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},v_i\tilde{v_j},1 \le i,j \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Unique KMS state: tilde M = M' but corner not an algebra
nodes.statement:
Going back to our starting 
example of unique KMS state for the automorphisms $\beta_t(s_i)= ts_i,\;t \in S^1$, we check that $v^*_k=S^*_k$,  
${\mathcal J} \tilde{v}^*_k {\mathcal J} = {1 \over d} S_k$ and thus equality holds i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$. But 
the corner vector space $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_c=P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P$ generated by the elements 
$\{\tilde{v}_I\tilde{v}^*_J: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ fails to be an algebra.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Does M' = tilde M hold for every extremal psi and factor omega
nodes.statement:
(a) Does the equality ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ hold in general for an extremal element $\psi \in K_{\omega'}$ and 
a factor state $\omega$?
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: When is the corner space tilde M_c a *-algebra
nodes.statement: (b) When can we expect $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_c$ to be a $*$-algebra and so equal to $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$?
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Proposition 3.2 (factoriality and gauge groups of the amalgamated representation)
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$ and $\psi$ be an extremal point in $K_{\omega'}$. 
We consider the amalgamated representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes
{\mathcal O}_d$ in $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ where the Popescu's elements $({\mathcal K},{\mathcal M},v_k,\;1 \le k \le d)$ are 
taken as in Proposition 2.4. Then the following statements hold:

\vskip 1em
\noindent (a) $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. Furthermore $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ 
and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors and the following sets are equal:

\noindent (i) $H=\{ z \in S^1: \psi \beta_z = \psi \}$;

\noindent (ii) $H_{\pi}  = \{ z : \beta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphisms of } \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$;

\noindent (iii) $\tilde{H}_{\pi}= \{ z : \beta_z \mbox{ extends to an automorphisms of } \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'' \}$.
Moreover $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ and $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ are factors.

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (b) $z \rightarrow U_z$ is the unitary representation of $H$ in the Hilbert space $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ 
defined by
$U_z(\pi(\tilde{s}_j \otimes s_i )\Omega=\pi(z\tilde{s}_j \otimes zs_i)\Omega$
 
\vskip 1em  
\noindent (c) The commutant of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d )''$ is invariant by the canonical endomorphisms
$\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(X) = \sum_i \tilde{S}_iX \tilde{S}^*_i$. Same is true 
for each $i$ that the surjective map $X \rightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ keeps the commutant of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes 
\mbox{UHF}_d)''$ invariant. Same holds for the map $X \rightarrow \tilde{S}^*_iX\tilde{S}_i$.

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (d) The centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d )''$ is invariant by the canonical endomorphisms
$\Lambda(X)=\sum_i S_iXS_i^*$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(X) = \sum_i \tilde{S}_iX \tilde{S}^*_i$. Moreover for each $i$, the
surjective map $X \rightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ keeps the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes 
\mbox{UHF}_d)''$ invariant. Same holds for the map $X \rightarrow \tilde{S}^*_iX\tilde{S}_i$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: For a factor state and extremal psi, the amalgamated representation is irreducible, pi(O_d)'' and its dual are factors with the same gauge stabiliser H, and the commutant/centre of the UHF part is invariant under Lambda and its inverses.
assumptions: Let $\omega$ be a translation invariant factor state on ${\mathcal B}$ and $\psi$ be an extremal point in $K_{\omega'}$.
conclusions: (a) $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement:
$P$ being the support projection by Proposition 2.4 we have $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): 
\sum_k v_k x v_k^*= x\} = {\mathcal M}'$. That $({\mathcal M}',\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is ergodic follows from a general 
result [Mo1] ( see also [BJKW] for a different proof ) as $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic for a factor state
$\psi$ being an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (Proposition 2.6). Hence $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\tilde{\tau}(x)=x \} = \mathbb{C}$. Hence by 
Proposition 3.1, we conclude that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. That both $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ 
and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors follows trivially as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''={\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ 
and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$. 

\vskip 1em
By the discussion above we first recall that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation of 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$. Let $G = \{ z=(z_1,z_2) \in S^1 \times S^1: \beta_z \mbox{
extends to an automorphism }$ $\mbox{on}\; \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$ be the closed 
subgroup where
$$\beta_{(z_1,z_2)}(\tilde{s}_j \otimes s_i)=z_1 \tilde{s}_j \otimes z_2s_i .$$
By repeated application of the fact that $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and 
$S_i^*\Omega=\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega$ as in Proposition 3.1 (a) we verify that $\psi \beta_{(z,z)}=\psi$ 
on ${\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ if $z \in H$. For $z \in H $ we set unitary operator $U_z \pi(x \otimes y) \Omega 
= \pi(\beta_z(x) \otimes \beta_z(y))\Omega$ for all $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ and $y \in {\mathcal O}_d$. 
Thus we have $U_z\pi(s_i)U_z^*=z\pi(s_i)$ and also $U_z\pi(\tilde{s}_i)U_z^*=z\tilde{s}_i.$  By taking 
its restriction to $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ respectively we check that
$H \subseteq \tilde{H}_{\pi} $ and $H  \subseteq H_{\pi}$.

\vskip 1em
For the converse let $z \in H_{\pi}$ and we use the same symbol $\beta_z$ for the extension to an automorphism of
$\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. By taking the inverse map we check easily that $\bar{z} \in H_{\pi}$ and in fact $H_{\pi}$ is
a subgroup of $S^1$. Since $\lambda$ commutes with $\beta_z$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$, the canonical endomorphism $\Lambda$ defined
by $\Lambda(X) = \sum_k S_kXS_k^*$ also commutes with the extension of $\beta_z$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Note that the map
$\pi(x)_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} $ for $x \in {\mathcal O}_d$ is a well defined $*$-homomorphism.
Since same is true for $\bar{z}$ and $\beta_z\beta_{\bar{z}}=I$, the map is an isomorphism. Hence $\beta_z$ extends
uniquely to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ commuting with the restriction of the canonical endomorphism
on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|{\mathcal H}}$. Since $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ is a factor, we conclude as in Proposition 2.5 (a) that 
$z \in H$. Thus $H_{\pi} \subseteq H$. As $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is also a factor, we also have $\tilde{H}_{\pi} \subseteq H$. 
Hence we have $H=H_{\pi}=\tilde{H}_{\pi}$ and $\{(z,z): z \in H \} \subseteq G \subseteq H \times H$. 

\vskip 1em
For the second part of (a) we will adopt the argument used for Proposition 2.5. To that end we first note that $\Omega$
being a cyclic vector for the representation $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ in the Hilbert space $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $, 
by Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] (note that the proof only needs the cyclic property ) the representation of UHF$_d$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $ 
is quasi-equivalent to its sub-representation on the cyclic space generated by $\Omega$. On the other hand, by our hypothesis that $\omega$ is a 
factor state, Power's theorem [Pow] ensures that the state $\omega'$ (i.e. the restriction of $\omega$ to ${\mathcal B}_R$ which is identified here with $\mbox{UHF}_d$ ) 
is also a factor state on $\mbox{UHF}_d$. Hence quasi-equivalence ensures that $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor. We also note that
the argument used in Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] is symmetric i.e. same argument is also valid for $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$.
Thus $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ is also a factor. This completes the proof of (a). We have proved (b) 
while giving proof of (a).  


\vskip 1em
For $X \in {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$, as $\Lambda(X)$ commutes with $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ and
$\{ S_iS^*_j: 1 \le i,j \le d \}$ we verify by Cuntz's relation that $\Lambda(X)$ is also an 
element in the commutant of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ once 
$X$ is so. It is also obvious that $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ if 
$X$ is so. Thus $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. For the last statement consider the map $X \rightarrow S_i^*XS_i$
on $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ which is clearly onto by Cuntz relation (3). Hence 
we need to show that $S^*_iXS_i$ is an element in the commutant whenever $X$ is so. To that end note that $S_i^*XS_i S_i^*YS_i=S_i^*S_iS_i^*XYS_i=S_i^*YXS_i=S^*_iYS_iS_i^*XS_i$ since $X$ commutes with $S_iS_i^*$. 
Thus onto property of the map ensures that $S_i^*XS_i$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. This completes the proof of (c) and (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Ergodicity of tau and tilde tau plus Proposition 3.1 give irreducibility; gauge groups compared via extensions as in Proposition 2.5; Powers' theorem and quasi-equivalence give factoriality.

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant algebra I
nodes.statement: One interesting problem here how to describe the von-Neumann algebra ${\mathcal I}$ which consists of invariant elements of the gauge action $\{ \beta_z: z \in H \}$ in ${\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Stormer's theorem on fixed-point algebras of compact group actions
nodes.statement:
A general result 
due to E. Stormer [So] says that the algebra of invariant elements is a von-Neumann algebra of type-I with 
centre completely atomic.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
conclusions: the algebra of invariant elements is a von-Neumann algebra of type-I with centre completely atomic

nodes.name: Spectral projections F_k of the gauge unitaries
nodes.statement:
Here the situation is much simple because we know explicitly 
that ${\mathcal I}=\{U_z: z \in H \}'$ and we write 
spectral decomposition as 
\begin{equation} 
U_z=\sum_{ k \in \hat{H} } z^k F_k
\end{equation} 
for $z \in H$, $\hat{H}$ is the dual group of $H$, either $\hat{H}=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ or $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:

nodes.name: Centre of I is generated by the F_k
nodes.statement: Thus the centre of ${\mathcal I}$ is equal to $\{F_k: k \in \hat{H} \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
