Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} F_0={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to 
conclude that $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_1=\Lambda({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_1$ and multiplying by ${\mathcal E}$ from left we get 
${\mathcal E}{\mathcal F} F_1={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_1$ as $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal E}={\mathcal E}$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated 
application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$. 

\vskip 1em 
If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly 
$\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \sum_k \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_k = \sum_k {\mathcal E} F_k = {\mathcal E}$ and also ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. 

\vskip 1em 
If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\mathbb{Z}$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and  
check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = 
\Lambda^k({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_0 - \Lambda^k({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_0= \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})(\tilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$
Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$.  


\vskip 1em
Now we are left to prove those three statements given in (b). $\omega$ being pure we have $P=Q$ and thus 
by Proposition 3.5 we have $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. We are left to show
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'=\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. For that we recall $F_0$ and check few obvious relation 
$F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0=F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0$.
Since $F_0\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_0$ is equal to $(\beta_z:z \in H)$ invariant elements in 
$F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and elements in $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$ are $(\beta_z: z \in H)$ invariant 
we conclude that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. Inclusion in other direction 
is obvious and thus Haag duality property (iii) holds.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: If-part via Arveson's asymptotics and Mohari's duality criterion. Only-if part: compare shifted support projections via Mackey imprimitivity and refute strict inclusion by a Hausdorff-maximality argument on chains of quasi-equivalent representations.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
(of Theorem 1.1:) (a) implies that $q_0=p_0$. (d) also says that $p_0=q_0$. Thus in either case, following last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6 we get $P=Q$. The statement (e) also implies $P=Q$. 
That shows now that (a),(d) as well as (e) implies (f) by the if part of Theorem 2.6 (a). That (b) implies (a) is trivial as $\Omega$ is separating for ${\mathcal M}_1,\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_1$ by faithful 
property. That (c) implies (f) is trivial as $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a factor. Thus we have showed so far any of the statement (a),(b),(c),(d),(e) implies (f). For the converse we appeal to
the only if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Each of (a)-(e) reduces to P=Q and hence purity via Theorem 3.6(a); the converse is the only-if part of Theorem 3.6.

nodes.name: Commutant is type-I and contains pi(B_L)''
nodes.statement:
A simple proof goes as follows: $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ being a type-I factor, its commutant 
is also a type-I factor. Thus we have an inclusion of type-I sub-factor $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: The commutant of a type-I factor is type-I, so pi(B_L)'' sits inside a type-I factor.

nodes.name: Normalise commutant to B(H^-)
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality we assume now that
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'={\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi})$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: WLOG identify the commutant with B(H^-).

nodes.name: Split H^- as tensor product
nodes.statement:
Now we again 
use type-I factor property of $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$ to write ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi} \equiv {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1) \otimes {\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)$ 
for two Hilbert spaces ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(k),\; k=1,2$ so that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'' \equiv {\mathcal B}({\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(1)) \otimes I_{{\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Use type-I property of pi(B_L)'' to factor H^- = H^-(1) tensor H^-(2).

nodes.name: Purity kills second factor
nodes.statement:
Since $\omega$ is pure we have 
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \bigcap \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)'=\mathbb{C}$ and so ${\mathcal H}^-_{\pi}(2)=\mathbb{C}$. Thus we arrive at 
our conclusion.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: Purity forces H^-(2) trivial, giving Haag duality.

nodes.name: Stinespring dilation of R
nodes.statement:
Following Popescu [Po] we define a completely positive map
$R: {\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ by
\begin{equation}
R(s_Is^*_J)=v_Iv^*_J
\end{equation}
for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$. The representation $S_1,..,S_d$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$ on ${\mathcal H}$ thus may be taken to be the Stinespring
dilation of $R$ [BR, vol-2] and uniqueness up to unitary equivalence follows from uniqueness of the Stinespring
representation. That ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the representation follows from the minimality property of the Stinespring
dilation.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Define the cp map R and take its minimal Stinespring dilation.

nodes.name: Part (a): Lambda^n(P) increases to I
nodes.statement:
For (a) let $Q$ be the limiting projection of $\Lambda^n(P)$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Then we have $\Lambda(Q)=Q$ i.e. $Q\Lambda(I-Q)Q=0$ 
and so $(I-Q)S_k^*Q=0$. Interchanging the role of $Q$ with $I-Q$, we get $QS_k^*(I-Q)=0$. This shows $QS_k^*=S_k^*Q$ for all $1 le k \le d$. 
Since $Q$ is a projection, taking adjoint in the relation, we get $Q \in \{S_k,S^*_k\}'$. That $Q \ge P$ is obvious since $\Lambda^n(P) \ge P$ 
for all $n \ge 1$. In particular $QS_If=S_If$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and $|I| < \infty$. Hence $Q=I$ by the
cyclicity of ${\mathcal K}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The limit projection is Lambda-invariant, commutes with S_k, and equals I by cyclicity.

nodes.name: Part (b): weak limit of Lambda^n(D)
nodes.statement:
For (b) essentially we deffer from the argument used in Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW]. We fix any $D
\in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and note that $P\Lambda_k(D)P=\tau_k(D)=D$ for any $k \ge 1$. Thus for any integers $n > m$
we have
$$\Lambda_m(P)\Lambda_n(D)\Lambda_m(P)=\Lambda_m(P\Lambda_{n-m}(D)P)=\Lambda_m(D)$$
Hence for any fixed $m \ge 1$ limit $<f,\Lambda_n(D)g>$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ exists for all
$f,g \in \Lambda_m(P)$. Since the family of operators $\Lambda_n(D)$ is uniformly bounded and $\Lambda_m(P) \uparrow I$
as $m \rightarrow \infty$, a standard density argument guarantees that the weak operator limit of $\Lambda_n(D)$ exists as
$n \rightarrow \infty$. Let $X'$ be the limit. So $\Lambda(X')=X'$, by Cuntz's relation, $X' \in \{S_k,S^*_k:1 \le k \le k \}'$.
Since $P\Lambda_n(D)P=D$ for all $n \ge 1$, we also conclude that $PX'P=D$ by taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$. Conversely,
it is obvious that $P\{ S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P \subseteq {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Hence
we can identify $P\{S_k,S^*_k:\; k \ge 1 \}'P$ with ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Lambda^n(D) has a weak limit X' in the commutant with PX'P=D.

nodes.name: Isometric order isomorphism
nodes.statement:
Further it is obvious that $X'$ is self-adjoint if and only if $D=PX'P$ is self-adjoint ( since $\Lambda^n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, 
by taking limit $\Lambda^n(PXP)=\Lambda^n(PX^*P)$ shows that $X^*=X$ if $D^*=D$ ). Now fix any self-adjoint element $D \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$. Since 
the identity operator on ${\mathcal K}$ is an element in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ for any $\alpha \ge 0$ for which $- \alpha P  \le D \le \alpha P$, we have $\alpha 
\Lambda_n(P) \le \Lambda_n(D) \le \alpha \Lambda_n(P)$ for all $n \ge 1$. By taking limit $n \rightarrow \infty$ we
conclude that $- \alpha I \le X' \le \alpha I$, where $PX'P=D$. Since operator norm of a self-adjoint element $A$
in a Hilbert space is given by
$$||A||= \mbox{inf}_{\alpha \ge 0}\{\alpha: - \alpha I  \le A \le \alpha I \}$$
we conclude that $||X'|| \le ||D||$. That $||D||=||PX'P|| \le ||X'||$ is obvious, $P$ being a
projection. Thus the map is isometrically order isomorphic taking self-adjoint elements of the commutant
to self-adjoint elements of ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich -alpha Lambda_n(P) <= Lambda_n(D) <= alpha Lambda_n(P) to get norm equality.

nodes.name: Part (c): equality when P in the bicommutant
nodes.statement:
We are left to prove (c). Inclusion is trivial. For the last part, we assume first that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For any element $D$
in ${\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\{S_k,S^*_k,\;1 \le k \le d\}'$ so that $PX'P=D$. Since $P$ commutes with $X'$, 
we verify that 
$$Dv^*_k= PX'PS^*_kP=PX'S^*_kP=PS^*_kX'P=PS^*_kPX'P=v^*_kD$$ 
We also have $D^* \in {\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ and thus $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Hence $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'$. Since $P\pi_{\hat{\omega}}
({\mathcal O}_d)'P = {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. Thus equality holds whenever
$P \in \{S_k,S_k^*,\;1 \le k \le d \}''$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: If P commutes with lifted elements, each tau-fixed D commutes with v_k.

nodes.name: Converse of (c)
nodes.statement:
For the converse note that by commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements
of the commutant $\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$.
Hence $P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Order isometry plus Proposition 4.2 of BJKW gives P in the bicommutant.

nodes.name: Intertwining part
nodes.statement:
For the proof of intertwining relation and their property we refer to main body of the proof of 
Theorem 5.1 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Refer to Theorem 5.1 of BJKW for the intertwiner statement.

nodes.name: Parts (a)-(c)
nodes.statement:
We fix a state $\psi$ and consider the GNS space  $({\mathcal H},\pi,\Omega)$
associated with $({\mathcal O}_d,\psi)$ and set $S_i=\pi(s_i)$. It is obvious 
that $S^*_kP \subseteq P$ for all $1 \le k \le d $, thus $P$ is the minimal subspace 
containing $\Omega$ and invariant by all $\{ S^*_k;\;1 \le k \le d \}$ i.e.
\begin{equation}
PS^*_kP=S^*_kP
\end{equation}
Thus $v^*_k=PS^*_kP=S_k^*P$ and so $\sum_k v_kv^*_k = \sum_k PS_kS^*_kP= P$ which is 
identity operator in ${\mathcal K}$. This completes the proof of (a) (b) and (c).
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: P is the minimal S_k^*-invariant subspace containing Omega, giving (a)-(c).

nodes.name: Part (d)
nodes.statement:
For (d) we note that
$$\psi(s_Is^*_J)$$
$$=<\Omega, S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$
$$=<\Omega,PS_IS^*_JP\Omega>$$
$$=<\Omega,v_Iv^*_J\Omega>.$$
Since ${\mathcal H}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega:|I|,|J| < \infty \}$ and
${\mathcal K}$ is spanned by the vectors $\{ S^*_J\Omega=v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$, 
${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for $S_I$ i.e. the vectors $\{ S_I{\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ spans 
${\mathcal H}$. Uniqueness up to isomorphism follows as usual by total property of vectors 
$v^*_I\Omega$ in ${\mathcal K}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Compute psi(s_I s_J^*) through P and deduce cyclicity of K.

nodes.name: Converse: dilate
nodes.statement:
Conversely for a Popescu's elements $({\mathcal K},v_i,\Omega)$ satisfying (a) and (b), we consider
the family $({\mathcal H},S_k,\;1 \le k \le d,P)$ of Cuntz's elements defined as in
Theorem 2.1.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Take the Cuntz family of Theorem 2.1 for the given Popescu elements.

nodes.name: Claim: Omega is cyclic
nodes.statement:
We claim that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow
S_i$. Note that by our construction vectors $\{S_If,f \in {\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total
in ${\mathcal H}$ and $v^*_J\Omega=S^*_J\Omega$ for all $|J| < \infty$. Thus by our hypothesis that
vectors $\{v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal K}$, we verify that
vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$. Hence $\Omega$ is a cyclic for
the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Show Omega is cyclic for the dilated representation.

nodes.name: Totality of S_I K
nodes.statement:
Note that by our construction vectors $\{S_If,f \in {\mathcal K}: |I| < \infty \}$ are total
in ${\mathcal H}$ and $v^*_J\Omega=S^*_J\Omega$ for all $|J| < \infty$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Recall S_I K is total and v_J^* Omega = S_J^* Omega.

nodes.name: Totality of S_I S_J^* Omega
nodes.statement:
Thus by our hypothesis that
vectors $\{v^*_J\Omega:|I| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal K}$, we verify that
vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega: |I|,|J| < \infty \}$ are total in ${\mathcal H}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Totality of v_J^* Omega gives totality of S_I S_J^* Omega.

nodes.name: Conclude cyclicity
nodes.statement:
Hence $\Omega$ is a cyclic for
the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$ of ${\mathcal O}_d$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Omega is cyclic.

nodes.name: Part (e): lambda-invariance
nodes.statement:
We are left to prove (e) and (f). It simple to note by (d) that $\psi \lambda=\psi$ i.e.
$$\sum_i <\Omega,S_iS_IS^*_JS^*_i\Omega>= \sum_i <\Omega,v_iv_Iv^*_Jv^*_i\Omega> $$
$$=<\Omega,v_Iv_J^*\Omega> = <\Omega,S_IS^*_J\Omega>$$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ where 
in the second equality we have used our hypothesis that the vector state $\phi$ on ${\mathcal M}$ 
is $\tau$-invariant.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: tau-invariance of phi gives psi lambda = psi.

nodes.name: Part (e): faithfulness
nodes.statement:
In such case we aim now to show that $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. To that end 
let $p'$ be the support projection in ${\mathcal M}$ for $\tau$ invariant state $\phi$. Thus $\phi(1-p') = 0$ 
i.e. $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and by invariance we also have $\phi(p'\tau(1-p')p')=\phi(1-p')=0$. Since $p'\tau(1-p')p' \ge 0 $ and an element in 
${\mathcal M}$, by minimality of support projection, we 
conclude that $p'\tau(1-p')p'=0$. Hence $p'\Omega=\Omega$ and $p'v^*_kp'=v^*_kp'$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. 
Thus $p'v^*_I\Omega=v^*_I\Omega$ for all 
$|I| < \infty$. As ${\mathcal K}$ is the closed linear span of the vectors $\{ v_I^*\Omega: |I| < \infty \}$, we conclude 
that $p'=p$. In other words $\phi$ is faithful on ${\mathcal M}$. This completes the proof for (e).
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The support projection of phi is tau-subharmonic and contains all v_I^* Omega, hence is 1.

nodes.name: Part (f): ergodicity transfer
nodes.statement:
We are left to show (f) where we assume that $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. $\Omega$ being a cyclic vector for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, the weak$^*$ limit of the increasing 
projection $\Lambda^k(P)$ is $I$. Thus by Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] we have $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic if and only if the reduced dynamics 
$({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: By Mohari's Theorem 3.6, ergodicity of the dilation equals ergodicity of (M,tau,phi).

nodes.name: Part (f): invariant projections are central
nodes.statement:
For the last part of the statement, we need to show for a projection $e \in {\mathcal M}$, $\tau(e)=e$ if and only if $e \in {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$.
It is an easy consequence since $\tau(e)=e$ says that $e\tau(I-e)e=0$ and so $(1-e)v_k^*e=0$. Changing the role of $e$ by $I-e$, we also get $ev_k^*(I-e)=0$ for
all $1 \le k \le d$. Thus we get that $e$ commutes with each $v_k$. $P$ being in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $v_k \in {\mathcal M}$. So $e \in {\mathcal M}'$. Thus by a standard theorem [La,Ev,Fr,BJKW] 
ergodic property is equivalent to factor property of ${\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: tau-invariant projections commute with v_k, so ergodicity is factoriality.

nodes.name: Sub-harmonicity of P
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Invariance gives Lambda(P) >= P, i.e. P S_k^* P = S_k^* P.

nodes.name: Reduced Markov map
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: phi is invariant for the reduced Markov map tau(x)=P Lambda(PxP) P.

nodes.name: Claim: Lambda^n(P) increases to I
nodes.statement:
We claim that $\mbox{lim}_{n \uparrow \infty}\Lambda^n(P)= I$. That $\{ \Lambda^n(P): n \ge 1 \}$
is a sequence of increasing projections follows from sub-harmonic property of $P$ and endomorphism
property of $\Lambda$. Let the limiting projection be $Y$. Then $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ and so $Y \in
\{S_k,S^*_k \}'$. Since by our construction, the GNS Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\hat{\omega}}}$ is
generated by $S_IS^*_J\Omega$, $Y$ is a scalar. $Y$ being a non-zero projection, it is
the identity operator in ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\psi}}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The limit projection is Lambda-invariant hence scalar, hence I.

nodes.name: Monotonicity
nodes.statement:
That $\{ \Lambda^n(P): n \ge 1 \}$
is a sequence of increasing projections follows from sub-harmonic property of $P$ and endomorphism
property of $\Lambda$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Lambda^n(P) increases by sub-harmonicity.

nodes.name: Limit lies in the commutant
nodes.statement:
Let the limiting projection be $Y$. Then $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ and so $Y \in
\{S_k,S^*_k \}'$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The limit Y is Lambda-invariant so commutes with S_k.

nodes.name: Limit is the identity
nodes.statement:
Since by our construction, the GNS Hilbert space ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\hat{\omega}}}$ is
generated by $S_IS^*_J\Omega$, $Y$ is a scalar. $Y$ being a non-zero projection, it is
the identity operator in ${\mathcal H}_{\pi_{\psi}}$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Cyclicity forces Y scalar, hence Y=I.

nodes.name: Parts (a)-(c) and first part of (d)
nodes.statement: Now it is routine to verify (a) (b) and (c). For the first part of (d) we appeal to Theorem 2.1.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Routine checks and Theorem 2.1.

nodes.name: M' equals tau-fixed points
nodes.statement:
For the last part
note that for any invariant element $D$ in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ there exists an element $X'$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ so that $PX'P=D$.
Since $P \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ we note that $(1-P)X'P=0$.
Now since $X' \in \{ S_k,S^*_k \}'$, we verify that $Dv^*_k= PXPS^*_kP=PXS^*_kP=PS^*_kXP=PS^*_kPXP=v^*_kD$. Since $D^* \in
{\mathcal B}_{\tau}({\mathcal K})$ we also have $D^*v^*_k=v^*_kD^*$. Thus $D \in \{v_k,v^*_k: 1 \le k \le d \}'={\mathcal M}'$. Since
$P\pi_{\hat{\omega}}({\mathcal O}_d)'P=
{\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau}$, we conclude that ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})_{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. The reverse inclusion is trivial.
This completes the proof for (d).
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Lift D to X' in the commutant; since P is in the bicommutant, D commutes with v_k.

nodes.name: Converse (i)
nodes.statement:
For the converse part: for (i), since by our assumption and the commutant lifting property self-adjoint elements of the commutant
$\{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}'$ is order isometric with the algebra ${\mathcal M}'$ via the map $X' \rightarrow PX'P$,
$P \in \{S_k,S^*_k,1 \le k \le d \}''$ by Proposition 4.2 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Order isometry and BJKW Proposition 4.2 give P in the bicommutant.

nodes.name: Converse (ii): cyclicity
nodes.statement:
For (ii) without loss of generality, we assume
that $\phi(x)=<\Omega,x\Omega>$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$ and $\Omega$ is a cyclic and separating vector for ${\mathcal M}$.
( otherwise we set state $\psi(s_Is^*_J)=\phi(v_Iv_J^*)$ and consider its GNS representation )
We are left to show that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation $\pi(s_i) \rightarrow S_i$. To that end 
let $Y \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ be the projection on the subspace generated by the vectors $\{S_IS^*_J\Omega:  
|I|,|J| < \infty \}$. Note that, $P$ being an element in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, $Y$ also commutes with all the elements of 
$P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P=P {\mathcal M} P$. Hence $Yx\Omega=x\Omega$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. Thus $Y \ge P$.  
Since $\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ by our construction, we conclude that $Y=\Lambda_n(Y) 
\ge \Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. Hence $Y=I$. In other words
$\Omega$ is cyclic for the representation $s_i \rightarrow S_i$. This completes the proof for (ii).
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: The projection onto the cyclic subspace dominates P and is Lambda-invariant, hence I.

nodes.name: Uniqueness
nodes.statement:
Uniqueness up to unitary isomorphism follows as GNS representation is determined uniquely up to unitary conjugation 
and so its support projection.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness from uniqueness of GNS representation.

nodes.name: Part (e): phi is tau-invariant
nodes.statement:
The first part of (e) we note that $PS_IS^*_JP=v_Iv_J^*$ for all $|I|,|J| < \infty$ and thus ${\mathcal M}=P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''P$ is the von-Neumann 
algebra generated by $\{v_k,v_k^*:1 \le k \le d \}$ and thus $\tau(x)=P\Lambda(PxP)P$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M}$. That $\phi$ is 
$\tau(x)=\sum_k v_kxv_k^*$ invariant follows as $\psi$ is $\lambda$-invariant. We are left to prove equivalence of statements (i)-(iii).
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: M is generated by v_k and phi is tau-invariant by lambda-invariance.

nodes.name: Part (e): ergodicity equals factoriality
nodes.statement:
By Theorem 3.6 in [Mo1] the Markov semi-group $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic if and
only if $(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'',\Lambda,\psi_{\Omega})$ is ergodic ( here we need to recall by (a) that
$\Lambda_n(P) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). By a standard result [Ev, also BJKW] $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$
is ergodic if and only if there is no non trivial projection $e$ invariant for $\tau$ i.e. ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} = \{e \in {\mathcal M}: e^*=e,e^2=e,\tau(e)=e \}=\{0,1 \}$. 
If $\tau(e)=e$ for some projection $e \in {\mathcal M} $ then $(1-e)\tau(e)(1-e)=0$ and so $ev^*_k(1-e)=0$. Same is true 
if we replace $e$ by $1-e$ as $\tau(1-e)=\tau(1)-\tau(e)=1-e$ and so $(1-e)v^*_ke=0$. Thus $e$ commutes with $v_k,v_k^*$ for all $1 \le k \le d$. 
Hence ${\mathcal I}^{\tau} \subseteq {\mathcal M} \bigcap {\mathcal M}'$. Inequality in the reverse direction is trivial and thus ${\mathcal I}^{\tau}$ is trivial if and only if ${\mathcal M}$ is a factor. 
This shows equivalence of (ii) and (iii) follows by a standard result [La,Fr] in non-commutative ergodic theory. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Invariant projections of tau are central, so ergodicity is equivalent to M being a factor.

nodes.name: Part (a)
nodes.statement:
It is simple that $H$ is a closed subgroup. For any fix $z \in H $ we define unitary operator $U_z$ 
extending the map $\pi(x)\Omega \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))\Omega$ and check that the map $X \rightarrow U_zXU^*_z$ extends $\beta_z$ 
to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. For the converse we will use the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a $\lambda$-invariant 
factor state and $\beta_z \lambda= \lambda \beta_z$ to guarantee that $\psi \beta_z (X) = {1 \over n} 
\sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \lambda^k \beta_z(X) = {1 \over n} \sum_{1 \le k \le n} \psi \beta_z \lambda^k(X) 
\rightarrow \psi(X)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for any $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, where we have used the same symbol $\beta_z$ 
for the extension. Hence $z \in H$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Implement beta_z by a unitary for z in H; conversely average over lambda to show invariance.

nodes.name: Pass to inductive limits
nodes.statement:
In the following instead of working with ${\mathcal O}_d$ we should be working with the inductive limit $C^*$ algebra and their inductive limit states. 
For simplicity of notation we still use $UHF_d,{\mathcal O}_d$ for its inductive limit of ${\mathcal O}_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} {\mathcal O}_d$ 
and $UHF_d \rightarrow^{\lambda} UHF_d$ respectively and so for its inductive limit states.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Work with inductive limit algebras and states.

nodes.name: Part (b): direct integral
nodes.statement:
Now we aim to prove (b). $H$ being a closed subgroup of $S^1$, it is either entire $S^1$ or a finite subgroup 
$\{exp({ 2i \pi l \over k})|l=0,1,...,k-1 \}$ where the integer $k \ge 1$. If $H=S^1$ we have nothing to prove 
for (b). When $H$ is a finite closed subgroup, we identify $[0,1)$ with $S^1$ by the usual map and note that 
if $\beta_t$ is restricted to $t \in [0,{1 \over k})$, then by scaling we check that $\beta_t$ defines a 
representation of $S^1$ in automorphisms of ${\mathcal O}^H_d$. Now we consider the direct integral representation 
$\pi'$ defined by
$$\pi'= \int^{\oplus}_{[0,{1 \over k})} dt \pi_{|_{{\mathcal O}^H_d}} \beta_t $$
of ${\mathcal O}_d^{H}$ on ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}\otimes L^2([0,{1 \over k})\;)$, where ${\mathcal H}_{|_{{\mathcal O}_d^H}}$ is the cyclic
space of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)$ generated by $\Omega$. That it is indeed direct integral follows as states
$\psi \beta_{t_1}$ and $\psi \beta_{t_2}$ are either same or orthogonal for a factor state $\psi$ (see the proof of Lemma 7.4 in [BJKW] for further details).
Interesting point here to note that the new representation $\pi'$ 
is $(\beta_t)$ co-variant i.e. $\pi' \beta_t=\beta_t \pi' $, hence by simplicity of the $C^*$ algebra ${\mathcal O}_d$ we 
conclude that $$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''^{\beta_t}$$
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: For finite H build a beta_t-covariant direct integral representation over [0,1/k).

nodes.name: Ergodic translation on L^infinity
nodes.statement:
By exploring the hypothesis that $\psi$ is a factor state, 
we also have as in Lemma 6.11 in [BJKW] $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;) \subset \pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''$. 
Hence we also have
$$\pi'({\mathcal O}_d^H)''= \pi({\mathcal O}_d^H)'' \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;).$$ 
Since $\beta_t$ is acting as translation on $I \otimes L^{\infty}([0,{1 \over k})\;)$ which being 
an ergodic action, we have 
$$\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})'' \otimes 1$$
Since $\pi'(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' \otimes 1$, we conclude 
that $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'' = \pi({\mathcal O}_d^{H})''$.
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Factoriality and ergodicity of translation give pi(UHF_d)'' = pi(O_d^H)''.

nodes.name: Part (c)
nodes.statement:
A proof for the statement (c) follows from Lemma 7.12 in [BJKW]. The original idea of the proof can be 
traced back to Arveson's work on spectrum of an automorphism of a commutative compact group [Ar1].
nodes.section: 2 States on ${\mathcal O}_d$ and the commutant lifting theorem
nodes.statement_short: Cite Lemma 7.12 of BJKW.

nodes.name: Parts (a), (b)
nodes.statement:
By our construction $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega =\tilde{v}^*_i\Omega=v_i^*\Omega=S_i^*\Omega$. Now (a) and (b) 
follow by repeated application of $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and
the commuting property of the two representation $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes I)$ and $\pi(I \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Repeatedly move tilde S_i^* Omega = S_i^* Omega across commuting representations.

nodes.name: Part (c): reduce to lifting
nodes.statement:
The last
statement (c) follows from a more general fact proved below
that the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is
order isomorphic with the set $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=x,\; \tilde{\tau}(x)=x \}= \{zI: z \in  \mathbb{C} \}$ via the 
map $X \rightarrow PXP$ where $X$ is the weak$^*$ limit of $\{\Lambda^m\tilde{\Lambda}^n(x)$ as $(m,n) \rightarrow 
(\infty,\infty)$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Reduce (c) to an order isomorphism of the commutant with joint fixed points.

nodes.name: Joint Lambda tilde Lambda limit is I
nodes.statement:
For details let $Y$ be the strong limit of increasing sequence of projections 
$(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^n(P)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. Then $Y$ commutes with $S_i\tilde{S}_j, S^*_i\tilde{S}^*_j$ 
for all $1 \le i,j \le d$. As $\Lambda(P)) \ge P$, we also have $\Lambda(Y) \ge Y$. Hence $(1-Y)S_i^*Y=0$. As $Y$ commutes 
with $S_i\tilde{S}_j$ we get $(1-Y)S_i^*S_i\tilde{S}_jY=0$ i.e. $(1-Y)\tilde{S}_jY=0$ for all $1 \le j \le d$. By symmetry 
of the argument we also get $(1-Y)S_iY=0$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Hence $Y$ commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and by symmetry of 
the argument $Y$ commutes as well with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. As $Yf=f$ for all $f \in {\mathcal K}$ and ${\mathcal K}$ is cyclic for the 
representation $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$ we conclude that $Y=I$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The limit of (Lambda tilde Lambda)^n(P) commutes with both representations and equals I.

nodes.name: Lift joint fixed points
nodes.statement:
Let $x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ so that $\tau(x)=x$ and $\tilde{\tau}(x) = x $ then as in the proof of Theorem 2.1 
we also check that $(\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P) \Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) (\Lambda \tilde{\Lambda})^k(P)$ is 
independent of $m,n$ as long as $m,n \ge k$. Hence the weak$^*$ limit $\Lambda^m \tilde{\Lambda}^n(x) \rightarrow X$ exists 
as $m,n \rightarrow \infty$. Furthermore the limiting element $X \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$ and $PXP=x$. That the 
map $X \rightarrow PXP$ is an order-isomorphic on the set of self adjoint elements follows as in Theorem 2.1. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Weak limits of Lambda^m tilde Lambda^n(x) give commutant elements compressing to x.

nodes.name: Irreducibility and factoriality
nodes.statement:
$P$ being the support projection by Proposition 2.4 we have $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): 
\sum_k v_k x v_k^*= x\} = {\mathcal M}'$. That $({\mathcal M}',\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is ergodic follows from a general 
result [Mo1] ( see also [BJKW] for a different proof ) as $({\mathcal M},\tau,\phi)$ is ergodic for a factor state
$\psi$ being an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (Proposition 2.6). Hence $\{x \in {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}): \tau(x)=\tilde{\tau}(x)=x \} = \mathbb{C}$. Hence by 
Proposition 3.1, we conclude that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$. That both $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ 
and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ are factors follows trivially as $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''={\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ 
and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Ergodicity of tau and its dual, then Proposition 3.1, gives irreducibility and factors.

nodes.name: H contained in H_pi and tilde H_pi
nodes.statement:
By the discussion above we first recall that $\Omega$ is a cyclic vector for the representation of 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)$. Let $G = \{ z=(z_1,z_2) \in S^1 \times S^1: \beta_z \mbox{
extends to an automorphism }$ $\mbox{on}\; \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'' \}$ be the closed 
subgroup where
$$\beta_{(z_1,z_2)}(\tilde{s}_j \otimes s_i)=z_1 \tilde{s}_j \otimes z_2s_i .$$
By repeated application of the fact that $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and 
$S_i^*\Omega=\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega$ as in Proposition 3.1 (a) we verify that $\psi \beta_{(z,z)}=\psi$ 
on ${\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ if $z \in H$. For $z \in H $ we set unitary operator $U_z \pi(x \otimes y) \Omega 
= \pi(\beta_z(x) \otimes \beta_z(y))\Omega$ for all $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d$ and $y \in {\mathcal O}_d$. 
Thus we have $U_z\pi(s_i)U_z^*=z\pi(s_i)$ and also $U_z\pi(\tilde{s}_i)U_z^*=z\tilde{s}_i.$  By taking 
its restriction to $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ respectively we check that
$H \subseteq \tilde{H}_{\pi} $ and $H  \subseteq H_{\pi}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Implement the diagonal gauge action by unitaries U_z.

nodes.name: H_pi contained in H
nodes.statement:
For the converse let $z \in H_{\pi}$ and we use the same symbol $\beta_z$ for the extension to an automorphism of
$\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. By taking the inverse map we check easily that $\bar{z} \in H_{\pi}$ and in fact $H_{\pi}$ is
a subgroup of $S^1$. Since $\lambda$ commutes with $\beta_z$ on ${\mathcal O}_d$, the canonical endomorphism $\Lambda$ defined
by $\Lambda(X) = \sum_k S_kXS_k^*$ also commutes with the extension of $\beta_z$ on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$. Note that the map
$\pi(x)_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} \rightarrow \pi(\beta_z(x))_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}} $ for $x \in {\mathcal O}_d$ is a well defined $*$-homomorphism.
Since same is true for $\bar{z}$ and $\beta_z\beta_{\bar{z}}=I$, the map is an isomorphism. Hence $\beta_z$ extends
uniquely to an automorphism of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ commuting with the restriction of the canonical endomorphism
on $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|{\mathcal H}}$. Since $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{{|}_{{\mathcal H}}}$ is a factor, we conclude as in Proposition 2.5 (a) that 
$z \in H$. Thus $H_{\pi} \subseteq H$. As $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is also a factor, we also have $\tilde{H}_{\pi} \subseteq H$. 
Hence we have $H=H_{\pi}=\tilde{H}_{\pi}$ and $\{(z,z): z \in H \} \subseteq G \subseteq H \times H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Extend beta_z commuting with Lambda and use factoriality as in Proposition 2.5(a).

nodes.name: UHF parts are factors
nodes.statement:
For the second part of (a) we will adopt the argument used for Proposition 2.5. To that end we first note that $\Omega$
being a cyclic vector for the representation $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ in the Hilbert space $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $, 
by Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] (note that the proof only needs the cyclic property ) the representation of UHF$_d$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} $ 
is quasi-equivalent to its sub-representation on the cyclic space generated by $\Omega$. On the other hand, by our hypothesis that $\omega$ is a 
factor state, Power's theorem [Pow] ensures that the state $\omega'$ (i.e. the restriction of $\omega$ to ${\mathcal B}_R$ which is identified here with $\mbox{UHF}_d$ ) 
is also a factor state on $\mbox{UHF}_d$. Hence quasi-equivalence ensures that $\pi(I \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is a factor. We also note that
the argument used in Lemma 7.11 in [BJKW] is symmetric i.e. same argument is also valid for $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$.
Thus $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes I)''$ is also a factor. This completes the proof of (a). We have proved (b) 
while giving proof of (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.11 of BJKW and Powers' theorem give factoriality of the UHF parts.

nodes.name: Parts (c), (d)
nodes.statement:
For $X \in {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$, as $\Lambda(X)$ commutes with $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ and
$\{ S_iS^*_j: 1 \le i,j \le d \}$ we verify by Cuntz's relation that $\Lambda(X)$ is also an 
element in the commutant of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d))''$ once 
$X$ is so. It is also obvious that $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ if 
$X$ is so. Thus $\Lambda(X)$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\lambda(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. For the last statement consider the map $X \rightarrow S_i^*XS_i$
on $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ which is clearly onto by Cuntz relation (3). Hence 
we need to show that $S^*_iXS_i$ is an element in the commutant whenever $X$ is so. To that end note that $S_i^*XS_i S_i^*YS_i=S_i^*S_iS_i^*XYS_i=S_i^*YXS_i=S^*_iYS_iS_i^*XS_i$ since $X$ commutes with $S_iS_i^*$. 
Thus onto property of the map ensures that $S_i^*XS_i$ is an element in the commutant/centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ once $X$ is so. This completes the proof of (c) and (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Cuntz relations show Lambda and X -> S_i^* X S_i preserve commutant and centre.

nodes.name: Cyclic subrepresentation is factor
nodes.statement:
Let $E' \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ be the projection onto the subspace generated
by the vectors $\{ S_IS^*_J\tilde{S}_{I'}S^*_{J'}\Omega,\; |I|=|J|,|I'|=|J'| < \infty \}$ and $\pi_{\Omega}$ be the restriction
of the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ to the cyclic subspace ${\mathcal H}_{\Omega}$ generated by
$\Omega$. Identifying ${\mathcal B}$ with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ we check that $\pi_{\omega}$ is unitary
equivalent to $\pi_{\Omega}$. Thus $\pi_{\Omega}$ is a factor representation.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The cyclic subrepresentation is unitarily equivalent to pi_omega, hence factor.

nodes.name: Central projections act by omega(E)
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Factoriality gives E E' = omega(E) E' and E E_0 = omega(E) E_0.

nodes.name: omega(E) is 0 or 1
nodes.statement:
Since $EE'$ is a projection and $E' \ne 0$, we have $\omega(E)=\omega(E)^2$. Thus $\omega(E)=1$ or $0$. So, for such an element $E$,
the following is true:
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: omega(E) is idempotent, giving the dichotomy below.

nodes.name: (i) Minimality of E_0
nodes.statement: (i) If $E \le E_0$ then either $E=0$ or $E=E_0$ i.e. $E_0$ is a minimal projection in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: E_0 is minimal central.

nodes.name: (ii) omega(E)=1 iff E >= E_0
nodes.statement: (ii) $\omega(E)=1$ if and only if $E \ge E_0$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Characterise omega(E)=1.

nodes.name: (iii) omega(E)=0 iff E E_0 = 0
nodes.statement: (iii) $\omega(E)=0$ if and only if $EE_0=0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Characterise omega(E)=0.

nodes.name: Lambda(E_0) equals or is orthogonal to E_0
nodes.statement:
As $\Lambda(E_0)$ is a projection in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by our last proposition i.e. Proposition 
3.2 (c), we have either $\omega(\Lambda(E_0))=1$ or $0$. Since $\Lambda(E_0) \neq 0$ by the injective property of the endomorphism, 
we have either $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$. In case $\Lambda(E_0) \ge E_0$ we have $S^*_iE_0S_i \le S^*_i\Lambda(E_0)S_i=E_0$ 
for all $1 \le i \le d$. If so, $S^*_iE_0S_i$ being a non-zero projection in the centre of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ (Proposition 3.2 (c) ), 
by (i) we have $E_0=\Lambda(E_0)$. Thus we have either $\Lambda(E_0)=E_0$ or $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: By Proposition 3.2(c), Lambda(E_0)=E_0 or Lambda(E_0)E_0=0.

nodes.name: Second iterate
nodes.statement:
If $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0$, we have $\Lambda(E_0) \le I-E_0$ and by Cuntz's relation we check that
$E_0 \le I - S^*_iE_0S_i$ and $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j \le I- S^*_jE_0S_j$ for all $1 \le i,j \le d$.
So we also have $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0 \le E_0- E_0S^*_jE_0S_jE_0=E_0$. Thus we have either
$E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0= 0$ or $E_0S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_jE_0=E_0$ as $S^*_jS^*_iE_0S_iS_j$ is an element
in the centre by Proposition 3.2 (c). So either we have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0) \le E_0$. 
$\Lambda$ being an injective map we either have $\Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^2(E_0)= E_0.$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: If orthogonal, Lambda^2(E_0) is orthogonal to or equal to E_0.

nodes.name: Induction on iterates
nodes.statement:
More generally we check that if $\Lambda(E_0)E_0=0, \Lambda^2(E_0)E_0=0,..\Lambda^k(E_0)E_0=0$ for some $k \ge 1$
then either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0$. To verify that first we check that in such a
case $E_0 \le I- S^*_IE_0S_I$ for all $|I|=n$ and then following the same steps as before to check that $S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_i
\le I-S^*E_0S_i$ for all $i$. Thus we have $E_0S^*_iS^*_IE_0S_IS_iE_0 \le E_0$ and arguing as before we complete the proof
of the claim that either $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)E_0=0$ or $\Lambda^{k+1}(E_0)=E_0.$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Inductively each Lambda^{k+1}(E_0) is orthogonal to or equal to E_0.

nodes.name: Orbit is orthogonal up to period
nodes.statement:
We summarize now by saying that $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..,\Lambda^{m-1}(E_0)$ are mutually orthogonal projections with $m \ge 1$ possibly 
be infinite, if not then $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: E_0, Lambda(E_0), ... are mutually orthogonal until the period m.

nodes.name: Restrictions pi_k
nodes.statement:
Let $\pi_k,\;k \ge 0$ be the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the
subspace $\Lambda^k(E_0)$. The representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ is 
isomorphic to the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to $E'$ and thus
quasi-equivalent. For a general discussion on quasi-equivalence we refer to section 2.4.4 in [BR vol-1]. Since $\omega$ is a factor state, 
$\pi_0$ is a factor representation.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define pi_k as restriction to Lambda^k(E_0); pi_0 is a factor representation.

nodes.name: Claim: each pi_k is a factor representation
nodes.statement:
We claim now that each $\pi_k$ is a factor representation. We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element 
in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element 
in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d). Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ 
for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$. 
Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. 
Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Pull central elements back to pi_0 by S_I^*.

nodes.name: Pull back to pi_0
nodes.statement:
We fix any $k \ge 1$ and let $X$ be an element 
in the centre of $\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$. Then for any $|I|=k$, $S^*_IE_kS_I=E_0$ and so $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element 
in the centre of $\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)$ by Proposition 3.2 (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: S_I^* X S_I is central for pi_0.

nodes.name: Scalar independent of I
nodes.statement:
Further $S_I^*XS_I= S^*_IXS_IS^*_JS_J = S^*_JXS_J$ 
for all $|J|=|I|=k$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation, we have $S^*_IXS_I= c E_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of the multi-index we choose $|I|=k$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Independence of multi-index and factoriality give a scalar c.

nodes.name: Reconstruct X
nodes.statement:
Hence $c \Lambda_k(E_0) = \sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IXS_IS_J^*=\sum _{|J|=k } S_JS^*_IS_IS_J^*X= X$ as $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)$. 
Thus for each $k \ge 1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation as $\pi_0$ is so.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Summing over J recovers X = c Lambda^k(E_0).

nodes.name: Lambda(E_0) = tilde Lambda(E_0)
nodes.statement:
We also note that $\Lambda(E_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0) \neq 0$. Otherwise we have $<S_i\Omega,\tilde{S}_j\Omega>=0$
for all $i,j$ and so $<\Omega,\tilde{S}_jS^*_i\Omega>=0$ for all $i,j$ as $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ commutes with 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. However $\tilde{S}^*_i\Omega=S^*_i\Omega$ and $\sum_i \tilde{S}_i\tilde{S}^*_i=1$ 
which leads a contradiction. Hence $\Lambda(E_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0) \neq 0$. As $\pi$ restricted to 
$\Lambda(E_0)$ is a factor state and both $\Lambda(E_0)$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0)$ are elements in the 
centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF})''$, by Proposition 3.2 (d), 
we conclude that $\Lambda(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}(E_0).$ Using the commuting property of the endomorphisms $\Lambda$ 
and $\tilde{\Lambda}$, we verify by a simple induction method that $\Lambda^k(E_0) = \tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ 
for all $k \ge 1$. Thus the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0, \tilde{\Lambda}(E_0),...$, are also periodic with same 
period or aperiodic according as the sequence of orthogonal projections $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),...$ is.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Non-orthogonality plus factoriality forces Lambda^k(E_0) = tilde Lambda^k(E_0).

nodes.name: Periodic case
nodes.statement:
If $\Lambda^m(E_0)=E_0$ for some $m \ge 1$ then we check that $\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} \Lambda^k(E_0)$ is a 
$\Lambda$ and as well $\tilde{\Lambda}$-invariant projection and thus equal to $1$ by the cyclic property of 
$\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. In such a case we set $V_z=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^kE_k$ for $z \in S^1$ 
for which $z^m=1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)= \sum_{0 \le k \le m-1}z^k\Lambda(E_k)=\sum_{0 \le k \le m-1} z^k E_{k+1}= \bar{z} V_z$ 
where $E_m=E_0$ and so by the Cuntz relations we have $V^*_zS_iV_z= \bar{z}S_i$ for all $1 \le i \le d$. Following the same 
steps we also have $\tilde{\Lambda}(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$ and so $V^*_z\tilde{S}_iV^*_z=\bar{z}\tilde{S}_i$ for $ 1 \le i \le d$. 
Thus $V_z=U_z$ for all $z \in H_0 = \{z: z^m=1 \} \subseteq H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The orbit sums to 1 and V_z implements the gauge action for z^m=1.

nodes.name: Aperiodic case: extend to Z
nodes.statement:
Now we consider the case where $E_0,\Lambda(E_0),..\Lambda^k(E_0),..$ is a sequence of aperiodic orthogonal
projections. We extend the family of projections $\{E_k:\;k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ to all integers by 
 
$$E_k=\Lambda^k(E_0)\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\; k \ge 1$$
and
$$E_k = S^*_IE_0S_I\;\; \mbox{for all}\;\;k \le 1,\;\;\mbox{where}\;\; |I|=-k$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Extend E_k to negative k by S_I^* E_0 S_I.

nodes.name: Claim: E_k well defined
nodes.statement:
We claim that the definition of $\{ E_k;\;k \le -1 \}$ does depends only on length of the multi-index 
$I$ that we choose. We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: 
$$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ 
where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, 
commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$. Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that 
$S_I\tilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have 
$$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JE_0\tilde{S}_J$$ 
for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: E_{-k} depends only on the length of I.

nodes.name: Independence of multi-index
nodes.statement:
We may choose any other $J$ so that $|J|=|I|$ and check the following identity: 
$$S^*_IE_0S_I = S^*_IE_0S_IS^*_JS_J=S^*_IS_IS^*_JE_0S_J=S^*_JE_0S_J$$ 
where $E_0$, being an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, 
commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ as $|I|=|J|$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Centrality of E_0 gives S_I^* E_0 S_I = S_J^* E_0 S_J.

nodes.name: Dual expression
nodes.statement:
Further $\Lambda^k(E_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(E_0)$ ensures that 
$S_I\tilde{S}_J^*$ commutes with $E_0$ for all $|I|=|J|=k$ and $k \ge 1$. Hence we also have 
$$E_{-k}=S^*_IE_0S_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JE_0\tilde{S}_J$$ 
for all $|J|=|I|=k$ and $k \ge 1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Also E_{-k} = tilde S_J^* E_0 tilde S_J.

nodes.name: Claim: Lambda shifts E_k
nodes.statement:
Now we claim that 
$$\Lambda(E_k) = \tilde{\Lambda}(E_k) = E_{k+1}$$ 
for all $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. For $k \ge 0$ we have nothing to prove. For $k \le -1$ we check that the following steps
$$\Lambda(S^*_IE_0S_I)$$
$$=\sum_j S_jS^*_iS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}S_iS_j^*$$
$$=\sum_jS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'} S_jS^*_iS_iS_j^* = S^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}$$
where we have $I=(I',i)$ and used the fact that elements $S_jS^*_i$ commutes with $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$, which are elements in the centre of 
$\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For a proof that 
$\tilde{\Lambda}(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ we may follow the same steps as 
$E_k=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$ where $|I|=-k$ and $k \le -1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Lambda(E_k) = tilde Lambda(E_k) = E_{k+1} for all k.

nodes.name: Nonnegative k
nodes.statement: For $k \ge 0$ we have nothing to prove.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Trivial for k >= 0.

nodes.name: Negative k
nodes.statement:
For $k \le -1$ we check that the following steps
$$\Lambda(S^*_IE_0S_I)$$
$$=\sum_j S_jS^*_iS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}S_iS_j^*$$
$$=\sum_jS^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'} S_jS^*_iS_iS_j^* = S^*_{I'}E_0S_{I'}$$
where we have $I=(I',i)$ and used the fact that elements $S_jS^*_i$ commutes with $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$, which are elements in the centre of 
$\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Compute Lambda(S_I^* E_0 S_I) using centrality.

nodes.name: Dual shift
nodes.statement:
For a proof that 
$\tilde{\Lambda}(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ we may follow the same steps as 
$E_k=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$ where $|I|=-k$ and $k \le -1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same steps with tilde S.

nodes.name: Orthogonality and completeness of E_k
nodes.statement:
We also claim that $\{ E_k: k \in \mathbb{Z} \}$ is an orthogonal family of non-zero projections. To that end we choose any two elements
say $E_k,E_m,\;k \ne m$ and use endomorphism $\Lambda^n$ for $n$ large enough so that both $n+k \ge 0 , n+m  \ge 0$
to conclude that $\Lambda^n(E_kE_m) = E_{k+n}E_{k+m}=0$ as $k+n \ne k+m$. $\Lambda$ being an injective map we get
the required orthogonal property. Thus $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k$ being an invariant projection for both $\Lambda$ and
$\tilde{\Lambda}$ we get by cyclic property of $\Omega$ that $\sum_{ k \in \mathbb{Z}} E_k=I$. Let $\pi_k,\; k \le -1$ be the representation $\pi$ 
of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ restricted to the subspace $E_k$. Going along the same line as above, we verify that for 
each $k \le -1$, $\pi_k$ is a factor representation of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Shift into nonnegative indices and use injectivity of Lambda; the sum is invariant hence I.

nodes.name: Gauge unitaries give H = S^1
nodes.statement:
We also set $V_z= \sum_{-\infty < k 
< \infty} z^k E_k$ for all $z \in S^1$ and check that $\Lambda(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$ and also $\tilde{\Lambda}(V_z)=\bar{z}V_z$. Hence $S^1=H$ 
as $H$ is a closed subset of $S^1$. This completes the proof of (a). Proof of (b) and (c) are now simple consequence of the proof of (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: V_z implements the gauge action for all z, so H = S^1; (b),(c) follow.

nodes.name: Pull back to F_0 and scalar by purity
nodes.statement:
Fix any $k \in \hat{H}$ and let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi'_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ then 
$S^*_IF_kS_I = S^*_I\Lambda^k(F_0)S_I = F_0$ as $S^*_JS_I$ commutes with $F_0$ for $|I|=|J|=k$ and further for any $|I|=|J|$, $S_I^*XS_IS_J^*S_J=S_I^*S_IS_J^*XS_J=S^*_JXS_J$ 
as $X$ commutes with $S_IS_J^*$ with $|I|=|J|$. Thus by Proposition 3.2 (c) $S^*_IXS_I$ is an element in commutant of $\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ 
for any $|I|=k$ and thus $S_I^*XS_I= c F_0$ for some scalar $c$ independent of $|I|=k$ as $\pi'_0$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Pull back by S_I; Proposition 3.2(c) and purity of pi'_0 give a scalar.

nodes.name: Reconstruct X
nodes.statement:
We use 
the commuting property of $X$ with $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ to conclude that 
$X = c \Lambda^k(E_0)$ for some scalar $c$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: X = c Lambda^k(E_0).

nodes.name: Negative k
nodes.statement:
If $k \le -1$ we employ the same method but with the endomorphism 
$\Lambda^{-k}$ so that $\Lambda^{-k}(X)$ is an element in the commutant of 
$\pi'_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Thus $\sum_{I:|I|=-k }S_IXS^*_I = c I$ and by 
the injective property of the endomorphism we get $X$ is a scalar. Thus we conclude that each $\pi'_k$ is 
pure if $\pi'_0$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Use Lambda^{-k} and injectivity.

nodes.name: k = 0
nodes.statement:
That $\pi'_0$ is quasi-equivalent to 
$\pi_0$ follows as they are isomorphic by construction.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: pi'_0 and pi_0 are isomorphic by construction.

nodes.name: E_k is the minimal central projection containing F_k
nodes.statement:
In the proof of Proposition 3.3 we defined representation $\pi_k$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ for all $k \in \hat{H}_0$ associated with minimal projections 
$\{E_k: k \in \hat{H}_0 \}$. More generally for any $k \in \hat{H}$, we denote $\pi_k$ for the restriction of $\pi$ to the minimal central projections 
$E_k$ on the subspace span by $\{\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'f: \forall \;\; f\;\; \in {\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}, \;\;F_kf=f \}$. 
So each $E_k$ is a minimal central element containing $F_k$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Each E_k is the minimal central projection containing F_k.

nodes.name: Minimal central projections coincide
nodes.statement:
However two such elements i.e. 
$E_k$ and $E_j$ are either equal or mutually orthogonal being minimal. Thus $\{E_k: k \in \hat{H} \} = \{E_k: k \in \hat{H}_0 \}$
and quasi-equivalence follows as $\pi_k$ is isomorphic with $\pi'_k$ for all $k \in \hat{H}_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Minimal projections are equal or orthogonal, so the families coincide and quasi-equivalence follows.

nodes.name: Finite H
nodes.statement:
First we consider the case when $H=\{z: z^n=1\}$. Projections $\Lambda(F'_0)$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are elements in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)'$ by Proposition 3.3. The representation $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ restricted to both the projections $\Lambda(F'_0),\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$ are pure as well. A pull back by the map $X \rightarrow S^*_iXS_i$ with any $1 \le i \le d$ will do the job for the projection $\Lambda(F'_0)$. Thus 
$\Lambda(F'_0)\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)\Lambda(F'_0) = c \Lambda(F'_0)$ for 
some scalar. By pulling back with the action $X \rightarrow S^*_i X S_i$ we get
$F'_0 S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i F'_0 = cF'_0$ and so 
$$c=<\Omega,S^*_i\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)S_i\Omega>$$
$$=\sum_k <\Omega,S_k S^*_iF'_0S_iS^*_k\Omega>$$
as $\tilde{S}^*_k\Omega=S^*_k\Omega$ and further $F'_0$ commutes 
with $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)$ and thus 
$$c=\sum_k <\Omega, S_k S_k^*\Omega>=1$$
This shows that $\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0) \ge \Lambda(F'_0)$. Interchanging the role
of $\Lambda$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we conclude that $\Lambda(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}(F'_0)$. Now it essentially follows along the same line  
$\Lambda^k(F'_0)=\tilde{\Lambda}^k(F'_0)$ for all $k \ge 1$. 
By Proposition 2.5 we also note that 
$$\Lambda^n(F'_0)=F'_0=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(F_0)$$ 
as $H=\{z : z^n =1 \}$. Thus $F'=\sum_{0 \le k \le n-1}\Lambda(F'_0)$ is a $\Lambda$ and as well $\tilde{\Lambda}$ invariant projection. Since 
$F'\Omega=\Omega$ we conclude by the cyclic property of $\Omega$ for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ that $F'=1$. Since $\Lambda^k(F'_0) 
\le F_k$ and $\sum_k F_k=1 $, we conclude that $\Lambda^k(F_0)=F_k$. In such a case we may check that  
$$F_k = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=n-k]$$ 
for $1 \le k \le n-1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Purity on Lambda(F'_0) gives Lambda(F'_0) = tilde Lambda(F'_0); summing the orbit gives F'_0 = F_0.

nodes.name: H = S^1
nodes.statement:
Similarly in case $H=S^1$ and $\omega$ is pure we also have $F_0=F'_0$ and 
for $k \ge 1$ 
$$F_k=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S_I\Omega: |I|= k]$$
$$F_{-k}=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''S^*_I\Omega: |I|=k]$$
Thus we have got an explicit description of the complete atomic centre of ${\mathcal I}$ 
when $\omega$ is a pure state.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same argument gives explicit F_k for the circle.

nodes.name: Part (a)
nodes.statement:
Along the same line of the proof of Proposition 2.5 (b) we get $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements 
in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ where factor property 
of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ is crucial as in proof of Proposition 2.5 (b). Same holds for $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ as 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is a factor. Here we comment that factor property of $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ can be
ensured whenever $\psi$ is an extremal element in $K_{\omega'}$ (See Proposition 3.2 (a) ).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: As in Proposition 2.5(b), using factoriality from Proposition 3.2(a).

nodes.name: Part (b): pure implies I = I_0
nodes.statement:
For (b) we will first prove ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ if $\omega$ is pure. As by definition ${\mathcal I}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}$, it is enough if we show 
${\mathcal I}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal I}'$. Let $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$ i.e. $X$ commutes with $\{ U_z:z \in H\}''$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 
\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. For each $k \in \hat{H}$, $F_kXF_k$ is an element in the commutant of $F_k\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 
\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$. $\omega$ being pure each representation $\pi$ restricted to $F_k$ is irreducible and thus
$F_kXF_k = c_k F_k$ for some scalars $c_k$. Hence $X=\sum_k c_k F_k \in {\mathcal I}'=\{U_z: z \in H \}''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Irreducibility on each F_k makes elements of I'_0 diagonal in F_k.

nodes.name: Part (b): I = I_0 implies pure
nodes.statement:
For the converse we need to show that the restriction of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 
\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ to $F'_0$ is pure. Let $X$ be an element on the subspace $F'_0$ and in the commutant 
of $F'_0\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F'_0$, ( which in our earlier notation $E'$ in Proposition 3.3 ). 
Then $X$ commutes with each $F_k$ for $k \in \hat{H}$ and $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 
\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_k$ as $F'_0 \le F_0$ and $F_k$ are orthogonal to 
$F'_0$ for $k \neq 0$. So $X$ commutes with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and 
$\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ i.e. $X \in {\mathcal I}'_0$. By our assumption ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$, we have now
$X \in {\mathcal I}'$ which is equal to $\{F_k: k \in \hat{H} \}''$ and so $X=cF_0$ 
for some scalar $c_0$. This shows that $F'_0=F_0$ and $\omega$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Commutant elements on F'_0 lie in I', hence scalar, so omega is pure.

nodes.name: Equivalence of (c), (d), (e)
nodes.statement:
\vskip 1em
(c) implies (d): $\{U_z: z \in H \}$ is a commuting family of unitaries such that $\beta_z(X)=U_zXU_z^*$ and 
thus by (c) $\{U_z: z \in H \}'' \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. Let $X$ be an 
element in the commutant of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''$. Then 
$X$ commutes also with $\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and thus $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by (c).
Hence $X$ is an element in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ and so 
$X=\sum_k c_kE_k$ where $E_k$ are the minimal projections in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ 
given in Proposition 3.3. However $X$ also 
commutes with $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ by our assumption (c) and $\Lambda(E_k)=E_{k+1}$ for $k \in \hat{H}$.  
So $c_k=c_{k+1}$ and $X$ is a scalar multiple of unit operator. Hence (d) follows from (c). Along the same line we prove 
(c) implies (e). For a proof for (d) implies (c) and (e) implies (c), we simply apply (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Commutant elements are central and Lambda-invariant, hence scalar.

nodes.name: Part (f): type-I
nodes.statement:
Now we will prove (f) and (g). That $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is 
a type-I von-Neumann algebra ( with completely atomic centre ) follows by a theorem of [So] once we use (c). In the proof 
of Proposition 3.3 we have proved that the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ is 
$\{U_z: z \in H_0 \}''$ where $H_0 \subseteq H$. For equality in the present situation we simply use (c), as $\beta_w(U_z)=U_z$
for all $w,z \in H$, to conclude that $U_z$ is in the centre of $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Stormer's theorem with (c) gives type-I with centre generated by U_z.

nodes.name: Part (g)
nodes.statement:
If (c) holds then ${\mathcal I}_0={\mathcal I}$ and thus (g) follows by (b). Here we will give another proof using the same idea to prove (f). 
Let $X$ be an element in the commutant of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, where $\pi_0$ is the factor 
representation on the minimal central projection $E_0$ defined in Proposition 3.3. Then $X$ commutes with 
$\{U_z: z \in H \}''$ and so by (c) $X$ in an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. 
So $X$ is in the centre of $\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\pi_0$ being a factor representation
$X$ is a scalar multiple of $E_0$. Thus $\pi_0$ is an irreducible representation and so $\omega$ is pure.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: pi_0 on E_0 is irreducible, so omega is pure.

nodes.name: Converse statement
nodes.statement:
By Proposition 3.1 we recall that $\pi'_0$ is unitary equivalent to the GNS representation of $({\mathcal B},\omega)$. 
Thus $\pi'_0$ is irreducible if and only if $\omega$ is pure. So for a pure state $\omega$, 
for each $k \in \hat{H}_0$, $\pi_k$ being quasi-equivalent to $\pi'_k$, $\pi_k$ is a type-I factor 
representation of $\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: For pure omega each pi_k is a type-I factor representation.

nodes.name: Part (a) and Lambda^n(E) increases to I
nodes.statement:
(a) is a restatement of Proposition 3.2 (a). ${\mathcal E}$ ( $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ ) being the support projection of
the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ ( $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ ) and $\psi = \psi \Lambda$ we have $\Lambda({\mathcal E}) \ge {\mathcal E}$ 
and further we have ${\mathcal E}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega] \ge [\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]$ and hence increasing projections in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$, 
$\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ because $\Omega$ is cyclic for $\pi({\mathcal O}_d \otimes \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ in ${\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ 
and limiting projection being in the commutant of $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ as well i.e. since $\Lambda(Y)=Y$ implies $Y \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ by Cuntz relations.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Restate Proposition 3.2(a); the support projection E is subharmonic with Lambda^n(E) to I.

nodes.name: Part (b)
nodes.statement:
We set von-Neumann algebras ${\mathcal N}_1=\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'{\mathcal E}$ and ${\mathcal N}_2=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''{\mathcal E}$. By our construction we have $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'' 
\subseteq \pi({\mathcal O}_d)' $ and so ${\mathcal N}_2 \subseteq {\mathcal N}_1$. Since $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ in strong operator topology, 
two operators in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ are same if their actions are same on ${\mathcal E}$. So (b) is true.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Operators of pi(O_d)' are determined by their action on E.

nodes.name: Part (c)
nodes.statement:
For (c) we note that $Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in {\mathcal N}_2 \subseteq {\mathcal N}_1$ and claim that $Q$ is the support projection of the state $\psi$ in ${\mathcal N}_2$. 
To that end let $x{\mathcal E} \ge 0$ for some $x \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ so that $\psi(QxQ)=0$. As $\Lambda^k(x{\mathcal E}) \ge 0$ for all $k \ge 1$ and $\Lambda^k({\mathcal E}) \rightarrow I$ 
we conclude that $x \ge 0$. As ${\mathcal E} \Omega=\Omega$ and thus $\psi(\tilde{{\mathcal E}}x\tilde{{\mathcal E}})=\psi(QxQ)=0$, we conclude
$\tilde{{\mathcal E}}x\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=0$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ being the support projection for $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. Hence $QxQ=0$.
As $\psi(Q)=1$, we complete the proof of the claim that $Q$ is the support of $\psi$ in ${\mathcal N}_2$. Similarly $Q$ is also
the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. This completes the proof of (c).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Show Q = E tilde E is the support of psi in pi(tilde O_d)'' E.

nodes.name: Part (d)
nodes.statement:
Thus if ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$, we get $\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \Lambda^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}})$ and 
${\mathcal E} \tilde{\Lambda}({\mathcal F}) = \tilde{\Lambda}(\tilde{{\mathcal E}})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and thus taking limit we get 
${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. It is obvious now that $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} = {\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}=Q$. This completes 
the proof of (d).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Take limits of Lambda^n to get F = tilde E and E = tilde F.

nodes.name: Corner factors M^1 and P in M^1'
nodes.statement:
As ${\mathcal E} \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ we check that von-Neumann algebras 
${\mathcal M}^1 = Q \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' Q$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 = Q \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d) Q$ acting on $Q$ satisfy 
$\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 \subseteq {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. Now we explore that $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)''= 
{\mathcal B}({\mathcal H} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} \tilde{{\mathcal H}})$ and note that in such a case $Q\pi( \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d )''Q$ 
is the set of all bounded operators on the Hilbert subspace $Q$. As ${\mathcal E} \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)''$ and 
$\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \in \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ we check that together ${\mathcal M}^1 = Q \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'' Q$ and 
$\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1 = Q \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d) Q$ generate all bounded operators on $Q$. Thus both ${\mathcal M}^1$ 
and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$ are factors. The canonical states $\psi$ on ${\mathcal M}^1$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1$ are 
faithful and normal. We set $l_k=QS_kQ$ and $\tilde{l}_k=Q\tilde{S}_kQ,\; 1 \le k \le d$ and recall 
that $v_k=PS_kP$ and $\tilde{v}_k=P\tilde{S}_kP,\; 1 \le k \le d$. We note that $Pl_kP=v_k$ and 
$P\tilde{l}_kP = \tilde{v}_k$ where we recall that, by our construction, $P$ is the support projection of 
the state $\psi$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''_{|}[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)\Omega]$. $Q$ being the support projection of 
$\pi({\mathcal O}_d)\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$, by Theorem 2.4 applied to Cuntz elements $\{S_i\tilde{E}: 1 \le i \le d \}$, 
$\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ is order isomorphic to ${\mathcal M}^{1'}$ via the map $X \rightarrow QXQ$. As the projection 
${\mathcal F}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\Omega] \in \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$, we check that the element $Q{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}Q \in {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. However 
$Q{\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal E}=QPQ=P$ and thus $P \in {\mathcal M}^{1'}$. We also check that 
${\mathcal M}^1\Omega={\mathcal M}^1P\Omega=P{\mathcal M}^1\Omega={\mathcal M} \Omega$ and thus $P=[{\mathcal M}^1\Omega]$. We set 
$\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ for the von-Neumann algebra generated by $\{\tilde{v}_k:\; 1 \le k \le d \}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: M^1 and tilde M^1 are commuting factors on Q and P lies in M^1'.

nodes.name: Reduce (e)(ii) to (e)(i)
nodes.statement:
So far our analysis did not use the hypothesis on statement (e) i.e. $P=Q$. For $P=Q$, we have 
${\mathcal M}^1={\mathcal M}$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}^1=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. By order isomorphic property 
we get (i) is equivalent to $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi({\mathcal O}_d)' \tilde{{\mathcal E}} = \tilde{{\mathcal E}} \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ 
and taking commutant again we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal E}} = \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. Now we invoke the first 
part of the argument changing the role or using the endomorphism $\tilde{\Lambda}$ we conclude that 
$\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$. This completes the proof of (e) provided we find a independent proof for (i) 
which is not so evident and this crucial point was not noticed in the proof given for Lemma 7.8 in [BJKW].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Under P=Q, (ii) follows from (i) by commutant lifting.

nodes.name: Endomorphism alpha and Takesaki route
nodes.statement:
Now we will analyze the representation $\pi$ of $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ which is pure to prove (i). To that end we note 
since $P=Q$ by our assumption, $\Omega$ is a common cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and ${\mathcal M}'$.   
Thus we can get an endomorphism $\alpha: {\mathcal M}' \rightarrow \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ defined by 
$$\alpha(y)=\tilde{{\mathcal J}}{\mathcal J} y {\mathcal J} \tilde{{\mathcal J}}$$ 
where $\tilde{{\mathcal J}}$ is the Tomita's conjugate operator associated with the cyclic and separating vector $\Omega$ for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$  
( i.e. for $y \in {\mathcal M}'$, we have ${\mathcal J} y {\mathcal J} \in {\mathcal M} \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$ since $\tilde{{\mathcal M}} \subseteq {\mathcal M}'$. 
Since $\tilde{{\mathcal J}}\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'\tilde{{\mathcal J}}=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$, we have $\alpha(y) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ ). We note that the general theory 
does not guarantee [AcC] that the endomorphism be Takesaki's canonical conditional expectation associated with $\phi$. If so then the modular 
automorphism group $(\sigma_t)$ of ${\mathcal M}'$ also preserves $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Thus $\sigma_z(x) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ for $-1 \le Im(z) \le 1$ 
if $x$ is an analytic element in $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Thus we would have got ${\mathcal J} v_k(\delta) {\mathcal J} = 
\sigma_{i \over 2}(\tilde{v}_k(\delta)) \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ where $x(\delta)$ is average of 
$\sigma_t(x)$ with respect to Gaussian measure with variance $\delta > 0$. That $\tilde{v}_k(\delta)$ 
is an analytic element follows from the general Tomita-Takesaki theory [BR1]. Since $v_k(\delta) \rightarrow v_k$ in strong 
operator topology as $\delta \rightarrow 0$ and ${\mathcal M} = \{v_k: 1 \le k \le d \}''$ together with 
${\mathcal J} {\mathcal M} {\mathcal J} = {\mathcal M}'$ we arrived at $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$. In the following we avoid this tempting 
route and aim to explore the general representation theory of $C^*$-algebras [BR1,chapter 2].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define alpha(y) = tilde J J y J tilde J into tilde M; avoid the Takesaki route.

nodes.name: Claim M' = tilde M: suppose not
nodes.statement:
We claim that ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Suppose not i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}} \subset {\mathcal M}'$. Then $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann subalgebras 
of $\alpha({\mathcal M}') \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}} $ being an into map and hence $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann 
sub-algebra of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$. Now consider the Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ and its dilation 
as in Theorem 2.1. Then by the commutant lifting theorem applied to pairs 
$(\tilde{v}_i),\alpha(\tilde{v}_i)$ we find a unitary operator $U$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ so that 
$U\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''U^*$ is strictly contained in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ ( Without loss of generality we can 
take the dilated Hilbert space for $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ to be same as $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ as there exists an 
isomorphism preserving ${\mathcal K}$, see the remark that follows after Theorem 2.1 ). We extend $U$ to a unitary operator 
on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ and denote $\pi_u(x)=U \pi(x) U^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ which 
is unitary equivalent to the pure representation $\pi$ and $\pi_u(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is strictly contained in 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. Now $\pi_u$ is also an amalgamated representation over the subspace ${\mathcal K}$ with
