$P_u=Q_u$. Thus we can repeat now same procedure with $\pi_u$ and so on. Note that the process won't terminate in finite 
time. Our aim is to find a contradiction from this using formal set theory.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: If tilde M is proper, unitary conjugation gives a strictly smaller dual algebra, repeating forever.

nodes.name: Proper subalgebra
nodes.statement:
Suppose not i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}} \subset {\mathcal M}'$. Then $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann subalgebras 
of $\alpha({\mathcal M}') \subseteq \tilde{{\mathcal M}} $ being an into map and hence $\alpha(\tilde{{\mathcal M}})$ is a proper von-Neumann 
sub-algebra of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: alpha(tilde M) is a proper subalgebra of tilde M.

nodes.name: Commutant lifting gives U
nodes.statement:
Now consider the Popescu elements $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ and its dilation 
as in Theorem 2.1. Then by the commutant lifting theorem applied to pairs 
$(\tilde{v}_i),\alpha(\tilde{v}_i)$ we find a unitary operator $U$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ so that 
$U\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''U^*$ is strictly contained in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ ( Without loss of generality we can 
take the dilated Hilbert space for $({\mathcal K},\alpha(\tilde{v}_i),\Omega)$ to be same as $\tilde{{\mathcal H}}$ as there exists an 
isomorphism preserving ${\mathcal K}$, see the remark that follows after Theorem 2.1 ).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Commutant lifting yields U with U pi(tilde O_d)'' U^* strictly inside.

nodes.name: Iterate
nodes.statement:
We extend $U$ to a unitary operator 
on $\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ and denote $\pi_u(x)=U \pi(x) U^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d$ which 
is unitary equivalent to the pure representation $\pi$ and $\pi_u(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ is strictly contained in 
$\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. Now $\pi_u$ is also an amalgamated representation over the subspace ${\mathcal K}$ with 
$P_u=Q_u$. Thus we can repeat now same procedure with $\pi_u$ and so on. Note that the process won't terminate in finite 
time. Our aim is to find a contradiction from this using formal set theory.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: pi_u is again an amalgamated representation with P_u=Q_u; the process does not stop.

nodes.name: Poset of quasi-equivalent representations
nodes.statement:
To that end we use temporary notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ defined in last paragraph and $\pi$ will be used for a generic representation. 
Let ${\mathcal P}$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d  
\rightarrow {\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H} )$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. 
$\omega(\pi(\theta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary 
equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus given an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ we can associate two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ 
and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$  $\pi_0$ being a pure representation, 
any element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ is a type-I factor representation of $\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d $. The interesting point here that $\displaystyle{\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P} }}\pi$ 
is also an element in ${\mathcal P}$ with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ 
if there exists an isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define the collection P of quasi-equivalent representations and the relation <.

nodes.name: (C1)
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Isometry maps cyclic vectors to cyclic vectors.

nodes.name: (C2)
nodes.statement: (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where ${\mathcal E}'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)'$;
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Isometry intertwines amplified representations.

nodes.name: (C3)
nodes.statement:
(C3) $U\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''U^* \subset \oplus_{1 \le 
\alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''E'_2$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Strict inclusion of dual algebras.

nodes.name: Strict partial order with infinite chain
nodes.statement:
That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega) \prec (\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. By our starting assumption that ${\mathcal M}' \neq \tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ 
we check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ there exists an element $\pi' \in {\mathcal P}$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. 
Thus ${\mathcal P}_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. 
If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The relation is a strict partial order and every element has a successor.

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality
nodes.statement: However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset ${\mathcal P}_0$ of ${\mathcal P}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximal chain P_0.

nodes.name: Claim: direct sum is an upper bound
nodes.statement:
We claim that 
$\pi_{max}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound 
in ${\mathcal P}_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists 
an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. 
By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_1 \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the 
required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} 
n_{\pi} \in \aleph_0$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$. This brings a contradiction 
as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ 
as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ is 
a proper subset of ${\mathcal M}'$. This completes the proof for (i) of (e) ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ when $P=Q$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: The direct sum is an upper bound in the chain, contradicting strictness.

nodes.name: Upper bound property
nodes.statement:
That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists 
an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Extend isometries to the direct sum.

nodes.name: Membership in the chain
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Maximality puts pi_max in P_0.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement:
This brings a contradiction 
as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ 
as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ is 
a proper subset of ${\mathcal M}'$. This completes the proof for (i) of (e) ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ when $P=Q$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: pi_max < pi_max contradicts strictness; hence M' = tilde M.

nodes.name: Part (f)
nodes.statement:
In the proof of ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ in (e), we have used equality $P=Q$ just to ensure that $\Omega$ is also a cyclic for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ and $P=Q$ is used 
to prove $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)' = \pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. So (f) follows by the proof of (e).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: (f) follows since P=Q was only used for cyclicity.

nodes.name: Part (g): set-up
nodes.statement: A proof for (g) is given in [Mo3] with ${\mathcal M}_0$. Here we will also give an alternative proof relating the criteria obtained in Proposition 3.4.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Give an alternative proof via Proposition 3.4.

nodes.name: Claim: tail algebra identity
nodes.statement:
To that end we claim that $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)')=\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'
\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'.$$ That $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \{ \tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J: |I|=|J| < \infty \}'$ follows by 
Cuntz relation and thus $\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap 
\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For the reverse inclusion let $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For $n \ge 1$, 
we choose $|I|=n$ and set $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$. 
We check that it is independent of the index that we have chosen as 
$Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_I\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_JX \tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JX\tilde{S}_J$ 
where in second equality we have used $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ and also 
$\Lambda^n(Y_n)=\sum_{|J|=n } \tilde{S}_J\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J=X$. This proves the equality in the claim.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Intersection of tilde Lambda^n(pi(UHF_d)') equals the relative commutant.

nodes.name: Inclusion
nodes.statement:
That $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \{ \tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J: |I|=|J| < \infty \}'$ follows by 
Cuntz relation and thus $\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap 
\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Cuntz relations give one inclusion.

nodes.name: Reverse inclusion
nodes.statement:
For the reverse inclusion let $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For $n \ge 1$, 
we choose $|I|=n$ and set $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Set Y_n = tilde S_I^* X tilde S_I.

nodes.name: Independence and reconstruction
nodes.statement:
We check that it is independent of the index that we have chosen as 
$Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_I\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_JX \tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JX\tilde{S}_J$ 
where in second equality we have used $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ and also 
$\Lambda^n(Y_n)=\sum_{|J|=n } \tilde{S}_J\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J=X$. This proves the equality in the claim.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Y_n is independent of I and Lambda^n(Y_n) = X.

nodes.name: Analogue for O_d
nodes.statement:
Going along the same line we also get 
$$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi({\mathcal O}_d)') = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes {\mathcal O}_d)'.$$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Same identity with pi(O_d)'.

nodes.name: Purity as asymptotic condition
nodes.statement:
By Proposition 3.4 $\omega$ is pure if and only if the set above is trivial. Thus once more by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] and 
Theorem 2.4 in [Mo2], purity is equivalent to asymptotic relation $||\psi \tilde{\tau}^n -\phi|| \rightarrow 0$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ 
for any normal state $\psi$ on ${\mathcal M}'$ ( Here we recall by Proposition 2.4 
$P\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'P={\mathcal M}'$ as $P$ is also the support projection 
in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''{\mathcal F}$ and support projection of $\phi_{\Omega}$ in $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'$ 
is ${\mathcal F}=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)''\Omega]$, where commutant is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$ ).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 3.4, Arveson and Mohari give purity iff ||psi tilde tau^n - phi|| -> 0.

nodes.name: Duality to tau
nodes.statement:
By a duality argument Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3] we conclude that $\omega$ is pure if and only if there exists 
a sequence of elements $x_n \in {\mathcal M}$ so that for each $m \ge 0$, $x_{m+n}\tau_n(x) \rightarrow \phi(x)1$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all $x \in {\mathcal M} \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. 
This completes the proof of (d) with ${\mathcal M}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Mohari's duality turns it into the x_n condition.

nodes.name: Version with M_0
nodes.statement:
For the proof with ${\mathcal M}_0$ we need to show if part as only if part follows ${\mathcal M}_0$ being a subset of ${\mathcal M}$ and $\tau$ 
takes elements of ${\mathcal M}_0$ to itself. For if part we refer to Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3].
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Only-if is immediate; if-part by Theorem 3.2 of [Mo3].

nodes.name: If-part: F = tilde E and E = tilde F
nodes.statement:
First we will prove that $\omega$ is pure if $P$ is also the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$, 
where $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]$. The support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and thus we also 
have $P = \tilde{{\mathcal E}}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ by our hypothesis. Since $\Lambda^n(P)=\Lambda^n({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} \uparrow {\mathcal F}$ and now
$\Lambda^n(P)=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}\Lambda^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \uparrow \tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, we also have 
${\mathcal F} = \tilde{{\mathcal E}}$. Similarly we also have for each $n$, ${\mathcal E}\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F})=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{{\mathcal E}})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ 
and thus taking limit we also get ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: From P = tilde E tilde F, limits of Lambda^n give F = tilde E and E = tilde F.

nodes.name: P = Q and cyclicity of tilde M
nodes.statement:
So we have $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}={\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}}=Q$. $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}=P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P$ is cyclic in ${\mathcal K}$ i.e. 
$[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=[P\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''P\Omega]= P\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=P{\mathcal E}=P$ as $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$.

nodes.name: Arveson asymptotics
nodes.statement:
However $\bigcap_{n \rightarrow \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)) = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'' \bigcap \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ ( for a proof which is a simple 
application of Cuntz relation, we refer to section 5 of [Mo2]). Further $\psi$ being a factor state in $K_{\omega'}$, by Proposition 3.2 $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is a factor. 
In particular we have $\bigcap_{n \rightarrow \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d))\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \mathbb{C} \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Thus by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] we conclude that $||\Psi \circ \tilde{\tau}_n -\phi|| \rightarrow 0$ 
as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all normal state $\Psi$ on $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0=P \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''P$ as $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ and support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ 
is $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and $P={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}{\mathcal E}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Trivial tail algebra and Arveson give ||Psi tilde tau_n - phi|| -> 0 on tilde M_0.

nodes.name: Gauge-invariant corners
nodes.statement:
Note that $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0 \subseteq {\mathcal M}_0'$ where ${\mathcal M}_0=P\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''P$. Further by Proposition 2.5 
${\mathcal M}_0 = \{x \in {\mathcal M}:\beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}\;\;\;$ and  $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0=\{x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}:
\beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}$. Once we set $P_0=[{\mathcal M}_0\Omega]$ then we also have $P_0=[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0\Omega]$ 
as $[\tilde{{\mathcal M}}\Omega]=P=[{\mathcal M}\Omega]$ by expending $u_z=\sum_{k \in \hat{H}} z^kP_k$ where $z \rightarrow u_z=
PU_zP$ is a unitary representation of group $H$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: M_0 and tilde M_0 are gauge-invariant parts with common cyclic projection P_0.

nodes.name: Duality and purity
nodes.statement:
For $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}, y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$ we have  
$$\phi(\tilde{\tau}(x)y)=\sum_k <\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega,x\tilde{v}^*_ky\Omega> = \sum_k <v^*_k\Omega,x y \tilde{v}^*_k\Omega>$$  
(as $v_k^*\Omega=\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega$ )
$$=\sum_k <\Omega, x v_kyv_k^* \Omega>=\phi(x \tau(y))$$
The dual group of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}},\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given on the commutant by 
$(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}',\tau,\phi)$ where $\tau(x)=\sum_k v_k x v_k^*$ for $x \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'$. 
where commutant is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K})$. 
Now moving to $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in the duality relation above, we verify that 
adjoint Markov map of $(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0,\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given by 
$(\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0,\tau,\phi)$ where $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$, the commutant of $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ 
is taken in ${\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$ and ${\mathcal K}_0$ is the Hilbert subspace $P_0$ with $\Omega$ as
cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ in ${\mathcal K}_0$. Thus by Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3], 
there exists a sequence of elements $y_n \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0$ such that for each $m \ge 1$, 
$y_{m+n}\tau_n(y) \rightarrow \phi(y)1$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ for all $y \in \tilde{{\mathcal M}}'_0 \subseteq {\mathcal B}({\mathcal K}_0)$. 
Thus $\omega$ is pure by Proposition 3.5 (e) once we recall ${\mathcal M}'=\tilde{{\mathcal M}}$ as $P=Q$ 
( and so ${\mathcal M}'_0 = \tilde{{\mathcal M}}_0$ ) by Proposition 3.5 (d). This completes the proof of
 purity property of $\omega$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Duality between tilde tau and tau plus Mohari's Theorem 2.4 and Proposition 3.5 give purity.

nodes.name: Only-if part: set-up
nodes.statement:
In the following we now prove the hardest part of the theorem namely $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ and ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ if $\omega$ is pure. Proof uses extensively 
the general theory of quasi-equivalent representation of a $C^*$ algebra and we refer [BR1, Chapter 2.4.4] as a general reference.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Prove tilde F = E and F = tilde E for pure omega.

nodes.statement_short: V implements the shift; E and tilde F are V-subharmonic.

nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Derive the subharmonic relations for E, tilde F, tilde E, F.

nodes.name: Shifted projections
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define E_n and tilde F_n.

nodes.name: Weak mixing of V
nodes.statement: Since $\beta_z(V)=V$ for all $z \in H$, $V \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by Proposition 3.4 as $\omega$ is pure. $\omega$ being also a factor state, we have $<f,V^ng> \rightarrow <f,\Omega><\Omega,g>$ as $n \rightarrow + \mbox{or} - \infty$ for any $f,g \in \pi({\mathcal B}_{loc})\Omega$ by Power's criteria [Pow] given in (1). Since such vectors are dense in the Hilbert space topology and the family $\{V^n:n \ge 1\}$ is uniformly bounded, we get $V^n \rightarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology as $n \rightarrow + \mbox{or} - \infty$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Powers' criterion gives V^n -> |Omega><Omega| weakly.

nodes.name: Assume H trivial
nodes.statement:
For the time being we assume that $H$ is trivial. Otherwise the argument that follows here we can use for the representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ i.e. $\pi$ restricted to $[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. 

\vskip 1em 
We have following distinct cases:
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to trivial H; two cases follow.

nodes.name: Case 1: E != I
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case 1.} ${\mathcal E} \neq I \;( \tilde{{\mathcal E}} \neq I)$. Let ${\mathcal E}_n \rightarrow {\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ as $n \rightarrow -\infty$ and thus $V{\mathcal E}_{-\infty}V^*={\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$. We claim that either ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty} = |\Omega><\Omega|$ or ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is a proper infinite dimensional projection i.e. if ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ is a finite projection then ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}=|\Omega><\Omega|$. Suppose not then the finite subspace is shift invariant. In particular there exists a unit  vector $f$ orthogonal to $\Omega$ such that $Vf=zf$ for some $z \in S^1$ and this contradicts weak mixing property i.e. $V^n \rightarrow |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology proved above as point spectrum of $V$ has only $1$ with spectral multiplicity $1$. 

\vskip 1em 
If ${\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$ is infinite dimensional we can get a unitary operator $U_0$ from 
$F_0=\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H}$ onto ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ and 
via the unitary map we can get a sequence of increasing projections $U_0{\mathcal E}_nU^*_0$ in ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ and note that $U_0{\mathcal E}_nU_0^*=V^nU_0 {\mathcal E} U_0^*(V^n)^*$. Note that if ${\mathcal E}_{- \infty}$ is infinite dimension the process will not stop in finite step. Thus we have $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{{\mathcal E}}} F(k)$ where the index set is either singleton or infinity and each $F(k)$ will give a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$, where $F(1)
=F_0-{\mathcal E}_{-\infty}$. Further $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ being a simple $C^*$-algebra, each such imprimitivity system 
is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ [Mo3,section 4]: We fix a nonzero $f \in {\mathcal E}-\theta^{-1}({\mathcal E}) \neq 0$ otherwise ${\mathcal E}=I$ as $\theta^n({\mathcal E}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. $\pi_f:x \rightarrow \theta^{-1}(x)f$ gives a representation of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d={\mathcal B}_L$ and we check that $[\pi_f(\theta^{-1}({\mathcal B}_L)''f] \le {\mathcal E}-\theta^{-1}({\mathcal E})$ 
as $f \perp [\theta^{-1}(\pi({\mathcal B}_R)')\Omega] \ge [\theta^{-1}(\pi({\mathcal B}_L))\Omega]$. Thus simplicity 
ensures that ${\mathcal E} - \theta^{-1}({\mathcal E})$ is a projection of dimension $\aleph_0$. Further $n_{\mathcal E}$ is either $1$
or $\aleph_0$ since $F_0$ is separable.   

\vskip 1em 
Since $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is also a proper projection, same argument is valid for $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ with $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_{-\infty}=
\mbox{lim}_{n \rightarrow -\infty} \theta^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}})$ i.e. we can write $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}} \tilde{H}(k)$, where each $\tilde{H}(k)$ give rises to a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$ where each system of imprimitivity is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ where $\tilde{F}(1) = F_0-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_{-\infty}$ 
and $n_{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$.        

\vskip 1em 
In the following we use temporary notation $H$ for Hilbert subspace $F_0$. For a cardinal number $n$, we 
amplify a representation $\pi:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(H)$ of the $C^*$ algebra ${\mathcal B}$ to $n$ fold direct sum 
$n\pi=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } \pi_k $ acting on $nH=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } H_k$  defining by 
$$n\pi(x) (\oplus \zeta_k) = \oplus (\pi(x)\zeta_k)$$ 
where $\pi_k = \pi$ is the representation of ${\mathcal B}=\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ 
on $H_k=H$ where $H =[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. We also 
extend $\bar{\tilde{F}} = \oplus \tilde{F}_{\alpha}$, $\bar{E} = \oplus E_{\alpha}$ and $\bar{V}=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n} V_k$ respectively. We also set notation $\Omega_k=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}\delta^k_j\Omega$. 

\vskip 1em 
Thus by Mackey's theorem, there exists a cardinal number $n \in \aleph_0$ and a unitary operator $U: nH \rightarrow nH$ so that 
$\bar{V}=U\bar{V}U^*$ and $\bar{{\mathcal E}}=U\bar{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}U^*$. We set a representation 
$\pi^U:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(nH)$ by $\pi^U(x)= Un\pi(x)U^*$
and rewrite the above identity as 
$$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n}
[\pi^U_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$
where $\pi^U_k(x)=U\pi_k(x)U^*$. Note that by our construction we 
can ensure $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ for all $1 \le k \le n$ as the operator 
intertwining between two imprimitivity systems are acting on the orthogonal 
subspace of the projection generated by vectors $\{\Omega_k:1 \le k \le n\}$. 

\vskip 1em 
We claim ${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Suppose not i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}$. In such a case we 
have
$$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n}
[\pi^u_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k]$$
Alternatively 
$$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n}
[\pi^u_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$

\vskip 1em 
Thus in principle we can repeat our construction now with $\pi^U$ and so we 
get a strict partial ordered set of quasi-equivalent representation of ${\mathcal B}$. 
In the following we now aim to employ formal set theory to bring a contradiction 
on our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}$. 

\vskip 1em 
To that end we need to deal with more then one representation of ${\mathcal B}$. For the rest of the proof we reset notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ used for the pure representation of 
${\mathcal B}$ in $H_0 =[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega_0]$ where $\Omega_0$ is the cyclic vector, the reset notation for $\Omega$. Let ${\mathcal P}$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ 
quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:{\mathcal B} \rightarrow {\mathcal B}(H_0)$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. $\omega(\pi(\theta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists 
minimal cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus for such an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega_{\pi})$ we can associate 
two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$  $\pi_0$ being a pure 
representation, any element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ is a type-I factor representation of ${\mathcal B}$. The interesting point here that $\displaystyle{\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P} }}\pi$ is also an element in ${\mathcal P}$ 
with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ if there exists an 
isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that 

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have 
$U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some 
$1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$;        

\noindent (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where ${\mathcal E}'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2({\mathcal B})'$; 
 
\noindent (C3) $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^1_{\alpha}] < \oplus_{1 \le 
\alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$.

\vskip 1em 
In the inequality we explicitly used that both Hilbert spaces are subspaces of $nH_0$ for some possibly larger cardinal 
number $n$. That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H,\Omega) \prec (\pi,H,\Omega)$ contradicts 
(C3) as $I=E_2'$. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. 
If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will 
do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$. Thus $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}$ and by our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \neq {\mathcal E}$ we also 
check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ there exists 
an element $\pi' \in {\mathcal P}$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus ${\mathcal P}_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain containing $\pi_0$.
 
\vskip 1em 
However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset ${\mathcal P}_0$ of ${\mathcal P}$ 
containing $\pi_0$. We claim that $\pi_{max} = \oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in ${\mathcal P}_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_{\pi_1} \rightarrow n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in {\mathcal P}_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph$. Thus by maximal property of ${\mathcal P}_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}$. This completes the proof that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ when ${\mathcal E} \neq I$. By symmetry of the argument we also get ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ when $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} < 1$.

nodes.statement_short: Mackey imprimitivity and a Hausdorff-maximality argument show tilde F = E.

nodes.name: Poset of quasi-equivalent representations
nodes.statement:
To that end we need to deal with more then one representation of ${\mathcal B}$. For the rest of the proof we reset notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ used for the pure representation of 
${\mathcal B}$ in $H_0 =[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega_0]$ where $\Omega_0$ is the cyclic vector, the reset notation for $\Omega$. Let ${\mathcal P}$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$

nodes.name: Strict partial order
nodes.statement:
In the inequality we explicitly used that both Hilbert spaces are subspaces of $nH_0$ for some possibly larger cardinal 
number $n$. That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H,\Omega) \prec (\pi,H,\Omega)$ contradicts 
(C3) as $I=E_2'$. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. 
If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will 
do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$. Thus $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}$ and by our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \neq {\mathcal E}$ we also 
check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in {\mathcal P}$ there exists 
an element $\pi' \in {\mathcal P}$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus ${\mathcal P}_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain containing $\pi_0$.

nodes.name: Claim: direct sum is an upper bound

That $\pi_{max} \in {\mathcal P}$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ there exists an element $(H_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in {\mathcal P}_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. nodes.name: Case 2: E = I
nodes.statement:
{\bf Case 2:} ${\mathcal E}=I \;(\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I)$. We need to show $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=I\;({\mathcal F}=I)$ respectively. Suppose not and assume that both $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper non-zero projection. 

\vskip 1em 
We set projection $G$ on the closed linear span of elements in the subspaces $[\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]$ for all $n \ge 0$. We recall that $\theta(X)=VXV^*$ 
where $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde{S}_k^*$ and $\theta^{-1}(X)=\tilde{\Lambda}(X)$ 
for $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. Thus we have 
$$V^*\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega$$
$$=\theta^{-n-1}({\mathcal F})V^*\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''V\Omega$$
$$=\theta^{-n-1}({\mathcal F}) \tilde{\Lambda}(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega.$$
Thus $(1-G)V^*G=0$ i.e. $\theta(G) \ge G$. It is also clear that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \le G$ 
as the defining sequence of subspaces of $G$ goes to precisely $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$ ( recall 
that $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})=\tilde{\Lambda}_n({\mathcal F}) \uparrow I$ strongly as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). Once more we have 
$\theta^n(G) \ge \theta^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \Lambda^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow 
\infty$.  

\vskip 1em 
If $G$ is a proper projection we can follow the steps as in the case 1 to find a unitary operator 
$U:nH \rightarrow nH$ with $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ and $U\bar{V}U^*=\bar{V}$ so that $U\bar{G}U^*=\bar{\tilde{{\mathcal F}}}$. 
We consider the subset ${\mathcal P}_G$ of elements in ${\mathcal P}$ for which ${\mathcal E}_{\pi}=1$ and 
$\{\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F}_{\pi}):n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_{\pi}$ 
and modify the strict partial ordering by modifying (C3) as  

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (C3') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] <  \oplus_{1 \le 
\alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$

\noindent So we also get $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}_G$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$ and going along the same line we conclude that 
$G=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Thus we conclude that $G$ is either equal to $1$ or $G=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. 

\vskip 1em 
\noindent {\bf Sub-case 1 of case 2:} If $G=I$ then ${\mathcal F} G = {\mathcal F}$ and so $[{\mathcal F}\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]={\mathcal F}$ as $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F}$. 
Thus $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \ge {\mathcal F}$. So $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \ge \tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F})$ for all $n \ge 1$ and taking limit we get $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} \ge I$ i.e. $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=I$. 
This contradicts our starting assumption that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper projection.  

\vskip 1em 
\noindent {\bf Sub-case 2 of case 2:} Now we consider the case $G=\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < I$. In such a case we have 
$(1- \tilde{{\mathcal F}})\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=0$ and so $\theta^{-n}({\mathcal F})$ commutes with $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ for all $n \ge 0$. 

\vskip 1em 
First we rule out the simplest possibility in the present situation for ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = |\Omega><\Omega|$. If so then $\omega$ is
a Bernoulli state and a proof follows once we compute the following using the property $\Lambda(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ i.e.
$\tilde{{\mathcal F}}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ 
and commuting property of ${\mathcal F}$ with $\pi(s_i)^*$ to get some scalars $\bar{\lambda_i}$ such
that 
$$\bar{\lambda}_i= {\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F} = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F}$$
and so 
$$\omega(s_Is_J^*)=<\Omega,\pi(s_I) \pi(s_J)^*\Omega>$$
$$=<\Omega, {\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} \pi(s_I)\pi(s_J)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F} \Omega>$$
$$=\lambda_I\lambda_J^*$$
The inductive limit state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, give rises to a pure state once restricted to ${\mathcal B}_R$ and thus we have 
${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ by Haag duality when $\pi({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor. This contradicts our starting assumption that ${\mathcal E}=I$.   

\vskip 1em 
Now we set projection ${\mathcal F}'$ defined by 
\begin{equation} 
{\mathcal F}'={\mathcal F}-{\mathcal F}\tilde{{\mathcal F}}+|\Omega><\Omega|
\end{equation} 
and check by commuting property of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ with ${\mathcal F}$ that 
$$ 
{\mathcal F}'\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}'){\mathcal F}' = (I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}){\mathcal F}\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F})(I-\theta^{-1}(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}))(I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}){\mathcal F} 
+ |\Omega><\Omega|$$ 
$$= {\mathcal F}(I-\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) + |\Omega><\Omega|={\mathcal F}'$$ 
where we have used $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) = \tilde{\Lambda}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F},\; \theta({\mathcal F}) \le {\mathcal F}$ and  
$\theta(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \Lambda(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) \ge \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. 
Thus we get 
\begin{equation} 
\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'
\end{equation}                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     

\vskip 1em 
We also rule out the possibility that ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = {\mathcal F}$. If so then ${\mathcal F} \le \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \le 
\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Taking limit we get $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=I$ as $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. 
This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis.  
  
\vskip 1em 
So we have in particular ${\mathcal F}' <  {\mathcal F} \le I$ and ${\mathcal F}' - |\Omega><\Omega| \neq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of ${\mathcal F}=I$ under our hypothesis $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$. 
Suppose so i.e. ${\mathcal F}=I$, then $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$ since $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \ge {\mathcal F}$. Then $Q={\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}} = {\mathcal E} = {\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= 
\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]={\mathcal E}$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$.    

\vskip 1em 
We also have $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'$ and $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F}$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements ${\mathcal F}',{\mathcal F},\theta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}},{\mathcal E},\theta$ 
to get a unitary operator $U:nH \rightarrow nH$ so that $U\bar{V}=\bar{V}U$ and $U\bar{{\mathcal F}}U^*=\bar{{\mathcal F}'}$ for a 
cardinal number $n$.    

\vskip 1em 
Now we consider a further subset ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ of ${\mathcal P}_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ 
of ${\mathcal B}$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: ${\mathcal F}_{\pi} < I, {\mathcal E}_{\pi}=I$ and $\{\theta^{-n}(\tilde{{\mathcal F}_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ 
commutes with ${\mathcal F}_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $({\mathcal H}_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec ({\mathcal H}_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ 
given by modifying condition (C3') as

\vskip 1em 
\noindent (C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] >  \oplus_{1 \le 
\alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$

\vskip 1em 
Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ by covariance relation 
of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can 
repeat the process and so ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$.   
Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption 
that ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F}$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis 
that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper projection i.e. ${\mathcal F} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Thus we arrive at $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ 
when ${\mathcal E}=I$.

nodes.name: Rule out Bernoulli case

First we rule out the simplest possibility in the present situation for ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = |\Omega><\Omega|$. If so then $\omega$ is

$$=<\Omega, {\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} \pi(s_I)\pi(s_J)^*\tilde{{\mathcal F}}{\mathcal F} \Omega>$$
$$=\lambda_I\lambda_J^*$$
The inductive limit state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$, give rises to a pure state once restricted to ${\mathcal B}_R$ and thus we have 
${\mathcal E}=\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ by Haag duality when $\pi({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a type-I factor. This contradicts our starting assumption that ${\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: If F tilde F = |Omega><Omega| then omega is a Bernoulli product state, contradicting E = I.

nodes.name: Projection F'
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Define F' and show theta^{-1}(F') >= F'.

nodes.name: Rule out F tilde F = F
nodes.statement:
We also rule out the possibility that ${\mathcal F} \tilde{{\mathcal F}} = {\mathcal F}$. If so then ${\mathcal F} \le \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \le 
\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{{\mathcal F}}) = \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$. Taking limit we get $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=I$ as $\tilde{\Lambda}^n({\mathcal F}) \uparrow I$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. 
This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise tilde F = I.

nodes.name: Rule out F = I
nodes.statement:
So we have in particular ${\mathcal F}' <  {\mathcal F} \le I$ and ${\mathcal F}' - |\Omega><\Omega| \neq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of ${\mathcal F}=I$ under our hypothesis $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$. 
Suppose so i.e. ${\mathcal F}=I$, then $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$ since $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} \ge {\mathcal F}$. Then $Q={\mathcal E} \tilde{{\mathcal E}} = {\mathcal E} = {\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'= 
\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}=[\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'\Omega]={\mathcal E}$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}} < {\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: F = I would give P = Q and tilde F = E via Proposition 3.5(e).

nodes.name: Mackey unitary for F, F'
nodes.statement:
We also have $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}') \ge {\mathcal F}'$ and $\theta^{-1}({\mathcal F}) \ge {\mathcal F}$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements ${\mathcal F}',{\mathcal F},\theta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $\tilde{{\mathcal F}},{\mathcal E},\theta$ 
to get a unitary operator $U:nH \rightarrow nH$ so that $U\bar{V}=\bar{V}U$ and $U\bar{{\mathcal F}}U^*=\bar{{\mathcal F}'}$ for a 
cardinal number $n$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Follow Case 1 with F', F, theta^{-1}.

nodes.name: Restricted poset
nodes.statement:
Now we consider a further subset ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ of ${\mathcal P}_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ 
of ${\mathcal B}$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: ${\mathcal F}_{\pi} < I, {\mathcal E}_{\pi}=I$ and $\{\theta^{-n}(\tilde{{\mathcal F}_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ 
commutes with ${\mathcal F}_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $({\mathcal H}_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec ({\mathcal H}_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ 
given by modifying condition (C3') as
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to representations with the extra commutation property.

nodes.name: (C3'')
nodes.statement:
(C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] >  \oplus_{1 \le 
\alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Reversed strict inequality.

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality contradiction
nodes.statement:
Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ by covariance relation 
of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in {\mathcal P}_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can 
repeat the process and so ${\mathcal P}_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$.   
Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption 
that ${\mathcal F}' < {\mathcal F}$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis 
that $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ is a proper projection i.e. ${\mathcal F} < {\mathcal E}=I$. Thus we arrive at $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E}$ 
when ${\mathcal E}=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Maximal chain argument contradicts F' < F, so tilde F = E when E = I.

nodes.name: Conclude for trivial H
nodes.statement:
By symmetry of argument used here it also follows that ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ when $\tilde{{\mathcal E}}=I$. This completes the proof of 
$\tilde{{\mathcal F}}={\mathcal E},\;\; {\mathcal F} =\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ for the case when $H$ is the trivial closed subgroup of $S^1$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: By symmetry F = tilde E; done for trivial H.

nodes.name: General H: notation
nodes.statement:
Now we will remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial using Proposition 3.4. Let $(H,\pi_0,\Omega)$ be the GNS space of the state $\omega$ on ${\mathcal B}$. 
Let $e_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_R)''$ and $\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''$ respectively. Similarly we also 
set projections ${\mathcal F}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal A}_R)''\Omega]$ and $\tilde{{\mathcal F}}_0=[\pi_0({\mathcal B}_L)''\Omega]$. We also set projections 
$q_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$ and $p_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Introduce support projections of omega in the GNS space.

nodes.name: Restrict to F_0
nodes.statement:
\vskip 1em 
$\omega$ being pure, by Theorem 3.4 any $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant element of ${\mathcal B}(\tilde{{\mathcal H}} \otimes_{{\mathcal K}} {\mathcal H})$ is an element in 
$\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. ${\mathcal E},\tilde{{\mathcal E}},{\mathcal F}, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}$ are $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ elements. Thus once 
we identify cyclic space $[\pi_0({\mathcal B})\Omega]$ with $F_0=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$, we get obvious relations 
\begin{equation} 
{\mathcal E} F_0=e_0,\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0=\tilde{e}_0,{\mathcal F} F_0=f_0, \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_0=\tilde{f}_0
\end{equation}
and 
\begin{equation} 
P F_0 = p_0 \;\;\mbox{and} \;\; QF_0=q_0
\end{equation}
as 
${\mathcal E}=[\pi(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega]$, $\tilde{{\mathcal E}} = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$, $Q={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$ and $P={\mathcal E} {\mathcal F}$. Further $V$ is also 
$\{ \beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant and $V \pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in {\mathcal B}$ which we have identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: By Proposition 3.4 gauge-invariant projections restrict to F_0 as e_0, f_0, ...

nodes.name: Apply trivial-H case
nodes.statement:
By applying the first part of the argument with representation $\pi_0$, for pure $\omega$, we have 
$e_0=\tilde{f}_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Get e_0 = tilde f_0, tilde e_0 = f_0, p_0 = q_0.

nodes.name: Propagate to F_m
nodes.statement:
Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as ${\mathcal E} {\mathcal F} F_0={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to 
conclude that $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_1=\Lambda({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_1$ and multiplying by ${\mathcal E}$ from left we get 
${\mathcal E}{\mathcal F} F_1={\mathcal E}\tilde{{\mathcal E}}F_1$ as $\Lambda({\mathcal E}){\mathcal E}={\mathcal E}$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated 
application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lambda repeatedly to get P F_m = Q F_m.

nodes.name: Finite H
nodes.statement:
If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly 
$\tilde{{\mathcal F}} = \sum_k \tilde{{\mathcal F}}F_k = \sum_k {\mathcal E} F_k = {\mathcal E}$ and also ${\mathcal F}=\tilde{{\mathcal E}}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Sum over F_k gives P = Q, tilde F = E, F = tilde E.

nodes.name: H = S^1
nodes.statement:
If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\mathbb{Z}$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and  
check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = 
\Lambda^k({\mathcal E})\tilde{{\mathcal E}} F_0 - \Lambda^k({\mathcal E}){\mathcal F} F_0= \Lambda^k({\mathcal E})(\tilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$
Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Use injectivity of Lambda for negative m.

nodes.name: Part (b)
nodes.statement:
Now we are left to prove those three statements given in (b). $\omega$ being pure we have $P=Q$ and thus 
by Proposition 3.5 we have $\tilde{{\mathcal M}}={\mathcal M}'$ and $\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'=\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''$. We are left to show
$\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'=\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. For that we recall $F_0$ and check few obvious relation 
$F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0=F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq F_0\pi({\mathcal O}_d)'F_0$.
Since $F_0\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_0$ is equal to $(\beta_z:z \in H)$ invariant elements in 
$F_0\pi(\tilde{{\mathcal O}}_d)''F_0$ and elements in $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)'$ are $(\beta_z: z \in H)$ invariant 
we conclude that $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_L)''$. Inclusion in other direction 
is obvious and thus Haag duality property (iii) holds.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: P = Q and Proposition 3.5 give (i), (ii); gauge invariance gives Haag duality (iii).

nodes.name: Heading
nodes.statement: (of Theorem 1.1:)
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Proof of Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: (a) gives p_0 = q_0
nodes.statement: (a) implies that $q_0=p_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: (a) gives q_0 = p_0.

nodes.name: (d), (e) give P = Q
nodes.statement: (d) also says that $p_0=q_0$. Thus in either case, following last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6 we get $P=Q$. The statement (e) also implies $P=Q$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Via the end of the proof of Theorem 3.6, (a), (d), (e) give P = Q.

nodes.name: Purity from P = Q
nodes.statement: That shows now that (a),(d) as well as (e) implies (f) by the if part of Theorem 2.6 (a).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 3.6(a) gives purity.

nodes.name: (b) and (c) imply (f)
nodes.statement:
That (b) implies (a) is trivial as $\Omega$ is separating for ${\mathcal M}_1,\tilde{{\mathcal M}}_1$ by faithful 
property. That (c) implies (f) is trivial as $\pi_{\omega}({\mathcal B}_R)''$ is a factor. Thus we have showed so far any of the statement (a),(b),(c),(d),(e) implies (f).
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: (b) gives (a); (c) gives (f) since pi(B_R)'' is a factor.

nodes.name: Converse
nodes.statement:
For the converse we appeal to
the only if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states:
nodes.statement_short: Only-if part of Theorem 3.6.
